Part of the fleet-wide OpenCode 2 migration tracked at https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/issues/374 (origin issue for the whole set).

Upstream migration guide: https://dev.opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/

Two workstreams in this repo:

## 1. Config validation — `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` against OpenCode v2

- Load the repo config with OpenCode v2 (`@opencode/cli@2.1.4`) and record what it accepts and rejects.
- Config files, agents, commands, and skills under `.opencode/` are intended to be compatible; some v1 fields are **accepted but ignored** by v2. Hard rejections get fixed (PR); accepted-but-ignored fields get listed here so we can decide whether to keep them while runtimes are still migrating or drop them.

Parent: #181

Backlog. Findings: `pkgs/mcpx/docs/opencode-plugin.md` §2 and §4.

**v1 plugins do not load in opencode v2** — no shim, no fallback (`packages/core/src/plugin/module.ts:60-73`). v2 needs a rewrite against `{id, setup}`, not a port.

What changes, each better than the v1 equivalent:

| v1 today | v2 |
| --- | --- |
| `shell.env` per command (carries sessionID) | `shell.create.before` has **no sessionID** → use `PUT /api/experimental/session/:id/environment` once per session |
| `experimental.chat.system.transform` | `session.hook("context")` → `event.system` (or a budgeted catalog in `event.tools`, diffed between turns) |
| `tool` map, un-namespaced | `tool.transform(e => e.add(...))` with a namespace |
| `tool.execute.after` sees success only | union on `status` — record failures too |

## What this is

Drew, 2026-10-29: find where OpenCode-native scheduled tasks can replace the Muse cron jobs that currently launch OpenCode — to save Muse tokens or raise throughput — with proper management and monitoring of those tasks and their outcomes. Study: ~/workspace/research_notes/opencode-scheduled-tasks-20261029/findings.md.

## Verdict: PARTIAL — the trigger exists, in OpenChamber, not OpenCode

- **OpenCode core has no scheduler.** Zero cron/timer code in packages/core|server|cli; sessions are purely event-driven.
- **OpenChamber has a real scheduled-tasks subsystem** (packages/web/server/lib/scheduled-tasks/): cron/daily/weekly/once with timezones, per-project + chats scopes, new-session-per-run (model/agent pinning, permission auto-accept, goal mode with token budget, sessions stamped metadata.kind='scheduled') or prompt-into-existing-session, cross-instance occurrence claiming, loop files (.agents/loops/*.md), REST + UI + CLI + an agent tool (openchamber_schedule).
- But it is a **prompt scheduler, not a job system**: state holds only the last run, no token capture, no alerting, in-code defaults of 4 global / 2 per-project concurrent runs, and a 30-minute run cap (vs ~90-minute shift windows).

**Wave 1 (~3.4B/day of the fleet's ~5.1B/day):**
1. **Repo-queue worker shifts — ~2.26B/day, save ~2.1–2.2B.** The Muse layer is claim/checkpoint/terminal-verbs via repo-queue.py plus implem

# Design mill: one fleet surface for OpenCode, OpenChamber, ID, and mcpx

Drew's design, dictated 2026-11-14. Protected design — do not close or drop without Drew.

## The idea in plain words

All automation and agent calls to OpenChamber, OpenCode, the ID binary, and the mcpx binary should go through subcommands of the fleet binary. At first this is mostly pass-through to the same underlying binary/endpoint, but fleet automatically resolves WHERE to talk: the right port on localhost, the right socket, the right endpoint path for that service on that host. Credentials are populated automatically and the caller can skip those fields. A raw mode (explicit endpoint path, raw POST body, explicit flag) always exists as an override.

This is a design mill with multiple passes, not one build. Passes are filed as sibling issues and cross-linked here.

## Cross-cutting rules Drew set

- Auto-resolution is the default; a specific flag overrides it. Defaults: the service's standard port on localhost or its socket.
- Endpoints can be customized per subprogram: a service may have a standard port, a website port, a homepage path, or a unique-ID custom path taken from settings, used raw.
- Everything exposed as a command should also be exposable as MCP and as REST (flag-gated, not all on at once). Later possibly GraphQL by the same switch.
- ID is the identity/transport layer of the whole system: many fleet commands will read/write the local or configured ID store, which may itself be remot
title: Design mill: one fleet surface for OpenCode, OpenChamber, ID, and mcpx

House rules: any schedule this creates lands its `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` row in the same PR; secrets by name only (Bitwarden at runtime, repo-archive pattern); builds/tests run via remote dispatch, never on the laptop or sandbox.

## Scope
The OpenCode session database joins the mesh. It is large on purpose (21.37 GB measured 2026-11-12, ~5.1 GB zstd) and has no scheduled off-laptop backup today (#10297, closed as the research tracker). Storage price is not the constraint; churn rate, restore time, and upload bandwidth are.

## Gate
This leg is **gated on research #9094** (OpenCode DB backup economics: measured churn, per-table growth model, costed comparison of full copy / zstd copy / restic deltas). Do not implement a scheme before #9094's comparison lands; the scheme choice is #9094's deliverable. When #9094 closes, this issue proceeds with the chosen scheme unmodified.

## Terms (from the design, whichever scheme #9094 picks)
- Targets: Google Drive + the laptop archive location (per the proto design §B); R2 joins only if #9094's costing says so.
- The DB is laptop-local state: it does NOT take a Turso home (size + churn break the appropriateness line, design §6).

## Acceptance

- [ ] One full backup cycle completes; size/time record

body:
## Symptom

Task 20708 (#3321 remainder, opencode lane, PR #12771 open, handed_off) is the only
candidate in every OpenCode claimant fire since the 2026-11-23 repair, and is never
launched:

- `repo-queue claim --handoff --platform openchamber` exits 5 ("no claimable task"),
  so claimant.py records `sink_claim_failed` / `cli_nonzero` each fire.
- `repo-queue claim --task 20708 --worker opencode-claimant` also exits 5.

## Cause

Lane ledger 10614 has `platform_limit = muse` with a recorded reason. In
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue/lifecycle.rs` `platform_limit_refusal`,
a valid limit refuses every family except its own, and refuses a claim that declares
no family. The ledger note says "the designated OpenCode claimant can still take the
row by id (platform is a mark for by-id claims)", but the code does not honour that:
the only claim that passes is one declaring `--platform muse`, which would misstate
the claimant's family.

Net effect: the opencode-lane designation (the reason the limit was set to muse) and
the claimant's family cannot both be satisfied, so the row is unreachable by the
opencode claimant.

## Ask

Decide the intended contract and make the code and ledger agree:
1. Should an opencode-lane handoff with a `muse` limit be claimable by the opencode
   claimant family? If yes, the limit names the wrong family or the claimant needs a
   sanctioned family/by-id exception.
2. Or clear the limit (or set it to `opencode`) so the opencode claimant can
title: claimant: opencode-lane task 20708 unclaimable after muse platform_limit repair (claim->refuse loop)

Drew's order (2026-11-13, main chat): in addition to using Whisper directly from the Cloudflare models, add Whisper (speech-to-text) and TTS into the OpenCode config, supporting routing pools, auto failover, and proper proxying to the model — possibly a pool for both directions.

Scope:
- Transcription models (Whisper family) and speech models (MeloTTS family) become first-class routable models in the OpenCode config, addressable through route pools like text models are today.
- Pools for both directions: a speech-to-text pool and a text-to-speech pool; evaluate one combined speech pool covering both directions and pick the shape that keeps direction/capability gating clean.
- Auto failover across providers carrying these models (Cloudflare Workers AI first; any other provider in the catalog carrying the same models joins as another door), with the standing routing rules (a 100%-walled leg is not attempted; failure skips to the next leg inside the same request).
- Proper proxying to the model: audio payloads pass through the route layer intact, with per-provider format translation where providers differ (the capabilities supplement's per-provider input-variance rule applies to audio too).
- Automatic silence removal in the OpenCode path as well as the Cloudflare-direct path: audio is trimmed / voice-activity-detected before transcription so silence is not billed or transcribed; for TTS, generated-audio duration is what is billed, so nothing extra is synthesized.
- Capability
title: OpenCode: Whisper STT + TTS as routed pool models — failover, proxying, silence auto-trim

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py` takes 43–100s wall with only ~2s CPU per run (measured 2026-11-23: 73.8s by the #13112 triage, 55–100s in the #13112 evidence, 74.2s / 43.5s in Lane OI's timed runs). The time is waits on sequential external reads: turso ledger SELECTs via the turso-exec helper, broker queue queries (claimed + handed_off per queue), and the OpenCode server session list over a 28k+ root-session store.

#13112 fixed the starvation symptom by raising claimant.py's gate timeout 30s -> 300s (PR #13134). That leaves the gate budget ~3x the observed worst case, but poll latency itself keeps growing with the session store, and every claimant fire pays it.

## Ask

Reduce poll.py's own end-to-end latency so the gate budget has durable margin:

- Parallelize the independent external reads (ledger bindings, per-queue claimed/handed_off rows, session list, active-id set) instead of running them strictly sequentially.
- Bound each external read with an explicit per-read timeout and a recorded slow-read note, so one slow backend degrades the poll visibly instead of silently eating the budget.
- Keep the output contract byte-compatible: claimant.py's cap counting delegates to poll.py's pinned functions (#6609), so the JSON shape and the pinned semantics (root = no parentID, activity = time.updated falling back to time.created, finished = time.idle or a top-level outcome) must not change.

## Acceptance

- poll.py timed over 10 runs on the laptop: p99 wall tim
title: perf(opencode-claimant): cut poll.py end-to-end latency (parallelize + bound its sequential external reads)

## Research — OpenCode DB backup economics + growth model

Parent program: #8983 · Feeds workstream B (backup mesh) · Proto design §B.

### Known (measured 2026-11-12, laptop production)

- `/home/user/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` = **21,368,037,376 B (19.9 GiB)**, ~448 MB internal freelist; **net allocated growth Nov 2 → Nov 12 = 0 bytes** (two dated full copies beside the DB are byte-identical in size); it was ~26 GB in the past and was pruned/vacuumed down. Drew: the DB stays large; do not propose shrinking it as the answer.
- Measured zstd sample ratio on raw pages: **23.8% (~4.2:1)** → full compressed copy ≈ **5.1 GB**.
- R2 Standard pricing $0.015/GB-month, egress free → at today's size: raw copy ≈ **$0.32/mo**, zstd copy ≈ **$0.08/mo**, restic compressed+dedupe retention set ≈ **$0.09–0.14/mo** (at an assumed 1–5% daily page churn — churn is UNMEASURED). Storage price is not the constraint; restore time and upload bandwidth are.
- Current backups: none scheduled/off-laptop. Manual `just opencode-db-backup` copies exist as a mechanism only.

### Research questions

1. **True churn rate:** measure daily changed-page volume (WAL/page deltas over ≥7 days) so the restic-delta size is evidence, not assumption.
2. **Growth model:** what drives growth (sessions/messages/parts/events/route tables), per-table sizes (dbstat timed out in the first pass — get it via a bounded method), and a 6–12 month projection under current fleet usage, including the freelist-absorption eff
title: research(atlas): OpenCode DB backup economics — copy vs zstd vs restic-delta cost + growth model

## Summary

opencode v2 wraps every MCP server in its own code mode unless the server is configured `codemode: false`, and this machine's v1 does the same because `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL` is set. So mcpx's `/mcp` ends up as a tool called from a program the model wrote for opencode's interpreter, and nothing in mcpx's docs says to opt out. v2 also appends `?codemode=false` to remote MCP URLs so servers that bundle code mode can expose raw tools; mcpx ignores it. opencode runs permission checks and plugin hooks per child call, shows live status, and cancels on abort. The plugin's `mcpx_exec` makes one blocking POST and ignores the abort signal (the session and field bugs are #189).

Found while writing the comparison register (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/`) and checked against the code at `05c78b2`. Each row below links its register entry, which carries the value, effort, risk, the specification text and every source.

Filed from Lane BG (Drew's order, 2026-11-22: "fix antigravity so it runs as acp in openclaw and opencode"). All evidence gathered live on the laptop 2026-11-22 ~19:40–20:00 CST.

### The agent itself is healthy

The Antigravity CLI (`agy` 1.5.9) ships a native ACP server (`agy acp`). Driven directly over stdio it completes a full round-trip with no auth ceremony (it uses the CLI's existing Google login; quota read tonight: weekly 0% used, resets 2026-11-30):

body:
## Gap

Drew's ruling (2026-11-03): a quota ask must terminate at the OpenCode server — not at a standalone proxy, and not at a credential store the server never sees. The Meta leg now complies: the quota gatherer (`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/gather-quota.ts`) asks the standing fork server's `GET /api/credential` (127.0.0.1:13420) for the credential, with the direct `opencode.db` read kept only as a transport-failure fallback (the quota CLI's combined-source shape, #2490).

The **OpenDesign leg cannot comply today**, and this issue names why precisely:

1. The OpenChamber quota module's OpenDesign provider (`server/lib/quota/providers/opendesign.js` in the OpenChamber fork) does not read the OpenCode credential machinery at all. It reads a **managed session credential** from OpenChamber's own quota credential store (`~/.config/openchamber/quota/opendesign.json`): a Better Auth session cookie plus a workspace id.
2. The usage API it answers from (`https://amr-api.open-design.ai/api/auth/get-session`, `.../v1/workspaces/:id/billing/coding-plan-usage`) accepts only that session cookie (`Cookie: better-auth.session_token=…` + `x-vela-workspace-id` header). Verified live 2026-11-03: the managed cookie returns 200.
3. The credential the OpenCode server holds for integration `opendesign` is the **AMR inference API key** (`type: key`, `sk-a…`). Verified live 2026-11-03: that key is refused by the billing/session API — **403 as a Bearer token and 403 presented as the session cookie**
title: quota(opendesign): billing quota ask cannot terminate at the OpenCode server — session-cookie credential the server cannot hold or use

body:
Fixes the reason the 2026-11-11 socket-adoption did not stick (#10639 fix ask 1).

## Root cause
Applying the Home Manager generation creates the `opencode.socket` unit and its `sockets.target.wants` link, but nothing ever *starts* the socket. systemd does not start newly-linked socket units on `daemon-reload`, and starting it while `opencode.service` owns 127.0.0.1:13420 fails to bind. So the declaration could land and the listener would stay in the server process forever.

Live evidence (2026-11-23 19:48Z): `~/.config/systemd/user/opencode.socket` is still an unmanaged regular file from Nov 10, there is no wants link, `UnitFileState=disabled`, and the listener is owned by the service process.

## Change
In `home/common/opencode-deploy.sh`, when the serving store path changed and the socket unit is enabled but inactive: stop the service, start the socket, then start the service so it adopts the socket's fd 3. If the socket fails to bind, the service is started directly (never left down). An unchanged store path still does nothing, so helper-only switches do not interrupt the server.

## Tests
`home/common/opencode-deploy.test.sh` gains a socket-handover case asserting the order stop service → start socket → start service, and the fake systemctl now models socket active/enabled state. All 6 cases pass locally.

## Remaining (live, on #10639)
The one-time cutover on the laptop and the three live acceptance invariants (same-build PID stability, changed-build port continuity, fu
title: fix(opencode): start opencode.socket before the build-change restart so handover sticks

Drew 2026-11-03: what does the bare `opencode-go` member do, and should it go?

It has no account of its own: no provider block in config (it's the built-in provider), no credential row under its own integration. A call to it rides whichever console login is currently active — today that's popesdrew — so its weight-1 share of the group was a second, unattributed draw on popesdrew's plan (the quota gatherer likewise reads bare `opencode-go` as combined rows, split into pools by credential label).

- `opencode-go-plans` members are now exactly the two accounts: `opencode-go.drewrypope` (3), `opencode-go.popesdrew` (2).
- Pool-level weights for the virtual target unchanged — each pool's aggregate Go share is unchanged; only the intra-group split is now fully attributed.
- The bare provider stays available for direct ad-hoc calls (it rides the active login, which is the right behavior interactively); it is simply no longer a pool member.

**Observed (2026-11-14, laptop amd):**
- The OpenCode server's session store is `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` — **21 GB**, live, plus `storage/` (3.1 GB) and `opencode-local.db` (14 MB) in the same tree (93 GB total including two 20 GB same-disk `.bak` copies and 26 GB of `tmp/`).
- No backup routine covers `~/.local/share/opencode`: `laptop-state-backup` covers `~/.local/state/opencode` (a different, 2.9 MB directory); `agent-backup` snapshots only `auth.json`/`opencode.jsonc`-class credential files, to a **local-only** plaintext directory (`~/.local/share/agent-backups`, latest 2026-11-14 09:36 — same disk).
- The two `.bak-2026-11-02` / `.bak-2026-11-11` copies of the DB are on the same disk and are not a backup.

**Consequence:** every live and historical OpenCode session (the fleet's working memory — prompts, tool results, session state that the PM claimant/dispatch flow binds to) exists exactly once. Partial reconstruction aids exist (Atlas extracts, Supabase session mirror per #3142, GitHub issue/queue records) but none restores the session DB itself.

Fixes #7780 · queue task 14560 (repo-health-code-pilot, lane code-g)

## Problem (traced to the code path, #7780)

`opencode.service` (fork module in developing-today-forks/opencode, `nix/modules`) runs with `Restart = "on-failure"` and no second-chance mechanism. On 2026-11-08 the restart attempt after a crash exited 0 in 731 ms without listening, systemd never retried, and port 13420 stayed dark ~15 minutes until a manual start. Nothing alerted.

## Why not `Restart = "always"`

The fork module chose `on-failure` deliberately: the service lifecycle hands a running server over to a successor during upgrades and the old process exits cleanly — a restart-on-success policy would spawn a second server racing the successor for the port. This PR takes the packet's watchdog option instead and preserves the handover semantics.

## Change

- New module `nixos/services/opencode-watchdog`: a per-minute systemd user timer + oneshot for user `user` on host `amd`.
  - Healthy (exit 0, darkness forgotten) when `opencode.service` is active **or** anything serves 127.0.0.1:13420 — a handover successor serving the port makes the watchdog healthy regardless of unit state, so it can never race a handover.
  - First dark sighting only stamps the time; dark windows shorter than the grace (default 120 s) are ignored — systemd restarts and handovers are dark only for seconds.
  - Dark continuously ≥ grace: logs an `ALERT` line, runs `systemctl --user start opencode.service`, and exits 1 so the watc
title: feat(opencode-watchdog): dark-port watchdog for opencode.service (code#7780)

## Fix for #9409: claim-stamp lookup honors the claimant tooling's OpenCode overrides

Codex's P2 on PR #9025, never addressed: `derive_claim_model_stamp` in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs` resolved the OpenCode server from `OPENCODE_SERVER_URL` and always loaded the production credential file (`~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json`), while the claimant tooling (`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py`, `poll.py`) uses `OPENCODE_URL` and `OPENCODE_AUTH_FILE`. With overrides configured, the lookup could contact a different server or authenticate with the wrong credentials — and its fail-soft return then silently left claims unstamped.

**Change** (client.rs only, +79/−7):
- `resolve_opencode_base_url(env_url, env_server_url)` — pure: `OPENCODE_URL` wins, then the legacy `OPENCODE_SERVER_URL`, then the shared loopback default `http://127.0.0.1:13420`; trims blanks/trailing slashes.
- `resolve_opencode_auth_file(env_file, home)` — pure: `OPENCODE_AUTH_FILE` wins, then the production state file under home.
- `derive_claim_model_stamp` uses both resolvers; its fail-soft contract is unchanged.

**Tests:** two new unit tests (`opencode_base_url_honors_claimant_overrides`, `opencode_auth_file_honors_claimant_override`) cover precedence, normalization, and defaults. Full suite: `cargo test -p fleet-queue --features queue-broker` = **308 passed** (306 baseline + 2 new).

## Implement: fleet OpenCode scheduled-task pattern (systemd timers + `opencode run`, per-job route)

Follow-on from the #2019 investigation (LIST 4a, fleet program #2055). The investigation's verdict: OpenCode has no native scheduler (upstream anomalyco/opencode#41906 still open); the proven pattern is an OS timer firing `opencode run --model opencode-route/<tier>` — verified live 2026-10-29 with a one-shot systemd user timer on the laptop (fired on schedule, route resolved to opencode-go DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, exit 0, zero Muse tokens in trigger or execution).

1. A small, committable job registry for fleet scheduled OpenCode tasks: one unit (or unit pair) per job under a managed directory, each naming cadence, workdir, prompt/command, and route (`opencode-route/workhorse|specialist|summit|speed`).
2. Per-job run logs in a fixed location, readable by the babysitter/monitor (directory-scoped server-API reads are the reliable session surface; `opencode session list` is not).

- Stall supervision: scheduling is not supervision. The preliminary-babysitter design is #2

body:
## Problem

When `pkgs/opencode-config-normalize/normalize.sh` repairs a config, its atomic temp-file replacement preserves the POSIX mode bits but drops file-specific extended ACL entries. A named user/group ACL on the original config is silently lost when the temp inode replaces it. If the directory has a default ACL, the new temp may inherit that default, but that is not the original file's ACL and does not preserve file-specific entries.

## Evidence (reproduced on current main)

- `normalize.sh:55` captures only `stat.S_IMODE(path.stat().st_mode)`.
- `normalize.sh:685-700` writes to a `tempfile.mkstemp` sibling, applies only `os.fchmod(..., original_mode)`, fsyncs, then `tmp.replace(path)`.
- Fixture: mode `0640`, ACL `user:1001:r--` and `mask::r--`; after a real repair, mode remains `640` but the named user ACL and ACL mask are gone. The repaired JSON content is correct.
- A second fixture confirmed a file-specific `user:1002:---` ACL disappears even when the directory supplies a default ACL; entries that reappear came from default-ACL inheritance on the new temp inode, not preservation of the original.
- `bash pkgs/opencode-config-normalize/normalize_test.sh` passes all 27 cases, including `mode-preserved` and `symlink-refused`; there is no ACL assertion.

A config may use an ACL to grant or restrict access for a specific local account independently of its mode bits. A successful normalization then silently changes that access policy. The file's cont

Closes #12223.

## What was wrong

`fetch_sessions()` escalated `SESSION_FETCH_LIMITS = (1000, 10000, 100000)`, but the OpenCode server caps `GET /api/session` `limit` at 200 (`MaxSessionsLimit = 200` in `packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts`). Every probe above 200 returned a 400, `_server_get()` swallowed the `HTTPError` into `None`, and every claimant fire ran blind: `cap_room` null, `stuck_bound` empty.

## The fix

- `fetch_sessions()` now requests pages at `limit=200` and follows the response envelope's opaque `cursor.next` until it is absent — completeness by construction, never requesting a limit above 200.
- `_server_get()` gained `raise_http_errors` so session-list reads surface a 400 instead of folding it into the silent-`None` transport/auth path. Callers already fail closed on exceptions (`claimant.py` wraps both fetch paths in `try/except` → unknown, never a partial list).
- The fail-closed rule is unchanged: any transport/auth failure or bad shape still yields `None`, which propagates as unknown cap room and no launches.

Closes #8039

Before: `claimant.py` had no lock, so a scheduled fire and an ad-hoc run could overlap (two fires 11 s apart on 2026-11-09). Each computed `cap_room` from the same active-root count, so together they could launch past the cap of 36 or race one candidate. The packet in `prompt.md` also claimed a parallel bounded pool that the code never had.

After: a fire holds an exclusive non-blocking `flock` on `~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/claimant.lock` (the file already existed and was unused). A second fire exits immediately with exit code 0 and logs `{"reason": "already_running"}`, with `candidates_seen` and `cap_room` null because it read nothing. The packet now says fires launch one at a time under that lock.

How: new `acquire_fire_lock()`; `main()` takes the lock, then runs the old body (now `_fire(mode)`) and releases the lock in `finally`. The kernel drops the lock if the process dies, so a crashed fire leaves no stale lock. Issue item 3 (real `candidates_seen`) already landed with #8038.

Testing: new `TestSingleInstanceLock` (second fire exits with `already_running` and never runs the fire; the lock is free after normal and raising fires). `python3 -I run_hermetic_tests.py`: 157 tests OK. `test_prompt_constants` OK.

## Directive (Drew, 2026-10-29 21:45 CDT, main chat)

"opencode shouldn't do work besides routing — it shouldn't do any loop etc."

## Problem

The opencode-route provider (#2250) currently serves each model request by creating a full OpenCode session and prompting it. That means the embedded OpenClaw agent's turn runs inside a second agent loop: OpenCode assembles its own context, tools, and plugins around a request that already carries OpenClaw's context. Two loops stacked — heavier, and the wrong ownership split.

## Required shape

For the MODEL door (OpenClaw embedded agent → opencode-route/*), OpenCode's job is routing only:

1. Resolve the route name (speed / workhorse / specialist / summit / scout) to a concrete pool member, using the existing route-pool state: weights, round-robin across workspaces, quota demotion, expiry.
2. Make a plain completion call to that member's provider endpoint with the member's credential.
3. Stream the response back to OpenClaw untouched (OpenAI-compatible, as today).
4. Record the attempt in the route ledger (route_attempt) exactly as the session path does, so quota accounting and demotion keep working.

No OpenCode session is created, no OpenCode agent loop runs, no OpenCode tools/plugins/context are applied. Loop ownership stays with the caller (OpenClaw embedded).

Out of scope: dispatch paths are different by design — ACP (#2256) and sessions_spawn (#2257) hand off whole tasks, and OpenCode doing the work there is the point.

## Symptom

The `sync-models` systemd **user service** on amd (Framework laptop) fails on every run. Latest journal evidence (2026-10-22 00:44:49 CDT, `journalctl --user -u sync-models`):

```
[sync-models] Discovered 22 models from Antigravity Language Server
[sync-models] Discovering Codex models...
[sync-models] Discovered 9 models from Codex cache
[sync-models] Error: /nix/.opencode/opencode.jsonc does not exist!
sync-models.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
```

Discovery works fine — the failure is purely in resolving the config file the script syncs models into.

## Root cause

`bin/sync-models.mjs` resolves the config relative to its own location:

```js
const ROOT_DIR = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..');
const OPENCODE_CONFIG_PATH = path.join(ROOT_DIR, '.opencode/opencode.jsonc');
```

That assumption holds in a repo checkout (`<repo>/bin` → `<repo>/.opencode/opencode.jsonc`). But the home-manager unit (`home/common/default.nix`, `systemd.user.services.sync-models`) runs the file from the Nix store: `node ${../../bin/sync-models.mjs}` interpolates to a lone store file (`/nix/store/<hash>-sync-models.mjs`), so `import.meta.dirname` is `/nix/store`, `ROOT_DIR` becomes `/nix`, and the script looks for `/nix/.opencode/opencode.jsonc` — which never exists.

(`POLICY_PATH` has the same store-layout problem, but its loader already tolerates a missing file and falls back to empty defaults, so it degrades silently instead of failing.)

## Fix
title: sync-models user service fails from Nix store layout: resolves opencode config to /nix/.opencode/opencode.jsonc

After: `opencode.inputs.mcpx-src` follows this flake itself (`follows = ""`). The opencode-bundled mcpx, its daemon modules, and the `packages.<system>.mcpx` here are all built from this repo's `pkgs/mcpx`. With the same fleet nixpkgs (all three fleet nodes lock 082bd9e7), that is one derivation, so a rebuild builds and tests mcpx once, and a fix landed here reaches amd's next rebuild without re-locking the fork.

Before: when `normalize.sh` repaired the opencode config, the atomic replace kept the mode bits but silently dropped any file-specific POSIX ACL entries. Under a directory default ACL the repaired file also picked up entries the original never had.

After: the repaired file carries exactly the original's access ACL, or none if the original had none. If the ACL can't be read, restored or verified, the config is left untouched and the script exits 1 instead of changing who can read it.

How: snapshot the raw `system.posix_acl_access` xattr (numeric ids) before the write, set it on the temp inode after `fchmod` (or remove an inherited one), read it back and check the mode, then rename. Platforms or filesystems without POSIX ACLs keep the mode-only behaviour, as the script header now documents. Two capability-gated cases in `normalize_test.sh` (`acl-preserved`, `acl-not-inherited`) set ACLs through the xattr directly, so no acl tooling is needed. Both fail on main (named user 65533 lost, default 65534 inherited) and pass here; all 27 existing cases still pass.

Refs #11836

## Summary

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py` reaches the laptop OpenCode server with HTTP Basic auth read from `~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json` (`_server_get`). `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` reaches the **same server on the same port with plain `curl -s` and no auth at all** — every one of its six server calls (session create, per-id get, messages, delete ×3).

Verified against `http://127.0.0.1:13420` on 2026-11-08:

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session
401
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session
401
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session/nope
401
  body: {"_tag":"UnauthorizedError","message":"Authentication required"}
$ curl -s -m 5 -o /dev/null ...   # curl exit status
0                                 # <- 401 is still a "successful" curl
```

## Consequences in the live path

1. **Session creation cannot succeed.** `POST /api/session` returns `{"_tag":"UnauthorizedError",...}` with no `id`. `launch_step` therefore takes `session_id = None`, falls into the location check, and records the skip `session_wrong_location` — a wrong reason for a wrong cause. Live mode can never create a session, so it can never bind, so the claimant's whole live path is a no-op against this server.
2. **`returncode == 0` is not a success test for the delete.** `supervision_step` gates its delet
title: opencode-claimant(claimant.py): every OpenCode server call is unauthenticated — session create always 401s, and the delete gate trusts curl's exit status

## Finding

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_slice1.sh` is described as a test, but unconditionally writes `live` to the user state mode file and runs the production claimant (`lines 72–78`). The claimant reads that same file in `claimant.py:166–177`; in live mode its `launch_step` proceeds past the shadow-only branch and can create sessions/bind tasks (`claimant.py:587–627`). The test only removes the mode file afterward (`test_slice1.sh:83`), so it can both perform real queue/session mutations and delete a pre-existing mode setting.

## Impact

Running this test on a developer laptop or CI host with access to the live queue can launch work or mutate task state. It is also not hermetic: it changes `~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/mode`, and the cleanup does not restore an existing value.

## Suggested fix

Refactor the test to use isolated temporary state and injected/mock queue/session dependencies. Keep any live-mode smoke check behind an explicit opt-in that cannot be enabled by the ordinary test target; preserve and restore any user state if a manual live check remains.
title: opencode-claimant tests can switch the real installation into live mode

Closes #11176

**Before:** a `model_route_windows` entry was checked at load only for its `start`/`end`. A typo elsewhere broke the gate without a word:
- an unknown `timezone` (`America/Chicagoo`) made the window never match;
- an unknown weekday (`"funday"`) was ignored, so the window still matched its other days;
- a string `daysOfWeek` (`"fri"`) widened the window to every day.

**After:** config load names each such window with its bad value, and the window fails closed (never active), the same as a bad time already does. Valid windows behave as before, including windows with no `timezone` or `daysOfWeek` and full weekday names like `"Wednesday"`.

**How:** a new `windowProblems(win)` checks start/end, timezone (an `Intl.DateTimeFormat` probe) and daysOfWeek (an array of weekday names). `warnInvalidWindows` prints its problems, and `windowActive` returns false when there are any.

**Testing:** `node --test bin/opencode-route-proxy.test.mjs` passes, 48 of 48. The new cases fail without the source change: the bad-timezone, string-days and unknown-day windows are named in the load log and never match, and a full weekday name still matches its day.

## Finding

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/run_hermetic_tests.py` (the claimant's canonical offline suite; the Makefile `test` target) currently exits 1 even when every test passes: `Ran 226 tests ... OK`, then `Forbidden external I/O attempted: subprocess.Popen ×5` and a failing exit status. The runner's contract is deliberate — code that catches the guard's exception still attempted real I/O, so the run is not a successful offline check — but five caught attempts across four modules trip it, so the suite cannot report green end-to-end.

Per-module bisect (2026-11-23, worktree bisect harness replicating the runner's guard/env, pristine main `ba7ea99e9fe`):

- `test_claimant.py` (offline_claimant): 2 attempts
- `test_babysitter.py` (offline_babysitter): 1 attempt
- `test_nudges.py` (offline_nudges): 1 attempt
- `test/test_claimant.py` (offline_mode): 1 attempt
- `test_poll.py`, `test_prompt_constants.py`: 0

Each attempt is a production fail-open path (a subprocess spawn whose failure the code under test catches and converts to a verdict) exercised by a test that does not fake the subprocess boundary.

## Suggested disposition

Per case, one of: fake the subprocess boundary in the test (the shape used for the `TestCodeSourceFireLog` fix landed under #13254), move the test out of the offline suite if its purpose is the spawn-failure path itself, or — only with a recorded rationale — amend the guard's contract. The suite should exit 0 with an empty violation list when this is done

## Observed

During the Nov 4, 2026 OpenCode claimant fire for #3026, two Workhorse sessions resolved to `antigravity-direct/claude-sonnet-5-5` and failed immediately after prompt delivery with `provider.invalid-request`:

> `tools.5.custom.input_schema: JSON schema is invalid. It must match JSON Schema draft 2020-12.`

The affected queue tasks were 1484 and 8706. Both sessions remain bound to their tasks and have a terminal failed outcome; no task work began. Other sessions from the same Workhorse route resolved to OpenAI and OpenCode Go models and continued normally.

## Expected

A Workhorse launch should either avoid incompatible tool schemas for this provider/model or fail over to a compatible route before leaving an already-bound queue task stranded.

## Impact

Repeated failures can leave claimed tasks bound to failed sessions. The claimant correctly does not relaunch over a bound session, so these need explicit recovery/watchdog handling.

## Investigation

Check which tool contributes the rejected custom input schema, whether it conforms to JSON Schema 2020-12, and whether the Antigravity provider path supports it. Then determine whether route eligibility or failover should exclude this provider/model for the affected tool set.
title: opencode-route/workhorse sometimes dispatches to schema-rejecting antigravity-direct

body:
Closes #6934.

`parseArgs` read `--db`/`--out-dir` values with an unguarded `argv[++i]`, so:
- a trailing `--db` set `args.db = undefined` and silently exported the default store (exit 0);
- `--db ""` did the same;
- `--db --out-dir <path>` swallowed the next flag and later threw `unknown argument: <path>`;
- a trailing `--out-dir` silently wrote to the default output directory.

Fix: a `parsePathFlag` helper in the #4739 invalid-argument style (mirroring `parseHourFlag`) rejects a missing, empty, or flag-like (`--…`) value for both flags with an `ExportError("invalid-argument", 2)` naming the flag and the bad value, thrown before any store read; the error carries the partially parsed args so `run()` still routes the failure document to a validly parsed `--out-dir`, and `run()` never throws for an argument error (PR #6810's restructure preserved). A present `--db` can therefore never silently fall back to `OPENCODE_USAGE_DB` or the default candidate list.

Tests: five new cases in `opencode-usage-export.test.mjs` — trailing `--db`, empty `--db` (with `OPENCODE_USAGE_DB` set, proving no env fallback), flag-like `--db`, trailing `--out-dir`, and a valid `--db`/`--out-dir` control. Full suite: **17 passed, 0 failed** (`node --test opencode-usage-export.test.mjs`, laptop).

## What

Corrects the re-enable condition written into the `_antigravity` comment in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` by PR #9857. Comment text only — the `"_antigravity"` entry in `disabled_providers`, every seat, and the provider definition are unchanged.

## Why

The original comment said to re-enable the door once the account is reinstated on appeal and a live probe answers. That condition is wrong and dangerous, per the findings on #9856:

- Google's appeal gives each account exactly **one** remediation.
- The terms ban accessing Antigravity through third-party software/wrappers outright.
- A single fleet call after reinstatement — even a probe — risks **permanent** suspension of the account.

The corrected comment states: `_antigravity` stays disabled for fleet use **permanently**, regardless of the appeal outcome; do not re-enable and do not probe; if the account is reinstated, it is for use inside Google's own Antigravity app only.

## Guards

Fixes #5016. Implements ruling `session-cap-5016` (recorded 2026-11-16T02:00:33-06:00 via orchestrator-audit-2026-11-16; agent note 6911818474 on #5016).

## What changes

The claimant concurrency cap is the **claimant's launch budget**: only claimant work roots consume slots. Scheduled fleet sessions — lane runners (`Queue lane (scheduled) - ...`), the claimant's own fire (`Opencode lane claimant/executor - ...`), sweeps and the conductor — are infrastructure outside the cap. They all carry `metadata.openchamber.kind == "scheduled"` on the OpenCode session (verified live 2026-11-16 across 366 roots); title prefixes are the fallback for legacy rows.

A server-active root whose `time.updated` has not moved for `ACTIVE_SET_STALE_MS` (2 h) is a zombie — #5016's ~18 h session — and releases its slot. Releasing a slot only changes cap accounting; it never kills a session.

- `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py`: `is_scheduled_session`, `is_claimant_root_session`, `count_active_claimant_roots`; staleness bound applied to active-set members in `_active_root_state`; `summarize_cap` / `get_active_root_session_count` count claimant roots.

## Problem

OpenClaw cannot run jobs carried by the OpenCode **workhorse route** (`opencode-route/workhorse`). Established in the OpenClaw-vs-OpenCode 1v1 round 2 (see #2171, comment 6493787758):

- `openclaw agent --model opencode-route/workhorse` → `Unknown model`. OpenClaw's only providers are four local OpenAI-compatible proxies — `agy` (:18743), `codex-proxy` (:18744), `design-code` (:18746), `commandcode` (:18748) — and **none fronts the OpenCode server**. OpenCode's server speaks its own session API, not the chat-completions shape OpenClaw providers use.
- ACP spawn tooling (`sessions_spawn` with runtime `acp`) is exposed only to non-sandboxed chat-channel sessions; both headless surfaces (CLI agent, embedded exec) run a restricted tool catalog without it. ## What happened (2026-11-08, laptop `amd`)

The standing OpenCode server (`opencode.service`, user unit, build 2.0.30+8ed9d6c, generation 548 pin) went down and stayed down for ~15 minutes until a human-path manual `systemctl --user start` restored it.

Timeline (all CST, from `journalctl --user -u opencode.service`):

- 12:53:05 — main process pid 2563072 exited with code 130 (SIGINT-style shutdown) after 11h37m uptime. Not OOM (no SIGKILL), not a systemd stop (would be SIGTERM), no NixOS switch (generation 548 untouched since 01:16), no sudo command in the journal at that minute. The sender of the SIGINT is not identifiable from the journal.
- 12:53:06 — systemd `Restart=on-failure` restarted the unit once (restart counter 1). The replacement process (pid 3770810) exited with status 0/SUCCESS after 731ms, producing no log output at all (no "server listening" line).
- Because the exit was "clean", systemd made no further restart attempt. Port 13420 had no listener and `~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json` was absent from then on.
- ~13:00 — a further process on a newer build (2.0.30+ae632cd, pid 3802432, per session-minder observation) wrote the service file, then exited and removed it. Also not a recovery.
- 13:01:26 — pm-aggregator reported "OpenCode server unreachable; attention empty"; the 13:01 collector wrote 0 sessions.
- 13:08:47 — manual `systemctl --user start opencode.service` with the unchanged unit/binary succeeded immediately: pid 3842555, listening on 1
title: opencode.service stays down: restart attempt exits 0 and systemd never retries

## What

Raises the opencode-claimant's poll gate timeout in `run_poll()` (`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py`) from 30s to 300s.

## Why (#13112)

poll.py's end-to-end latency measures 55–100s wall with ~2s CPU (sequential turso ledger reads + broker queries + the growing OpenCode session store), permanently above the hard-coded 30s gate timeout. Every live claimant fire failed closed as `gate_unknown` and launched nothing — 21 of the last 40 fires — while a real candidate (task 20708) waited unbound with cap_room=36.

## Regression note

The timeout side moved, not the poll side. 300s covers the aggregate of poll.py's per-call timeouts (15s server GET, 30s broker POSTs) plus session-store growth, ~3x margin over the observed ~100s worst case. Fail-closed behavior is unchanged: a poll exceeding 300s or exiting non-zero still ends the fire as `gate_unknown`. The single-instance lock keeps overlapping fires impossible, so a slow poll only delays a fire; it cannot double-launch. Reducing poll.py's own latency (parallelizing its independent reads) remains a separate follow-up.

## Provenance

Cherry-picked from the parked, never-pushed commit `8e472164d4cf` (branch `parked/opencode-claimant-poll-timeout-20261122` in the laptop primary), left unlanded by its author; landed here via worktree + PR for the #13112 acceptance.

Fixes #7927 (queue task 14574).

## Problem
Scheduled lane waves seat ~10 sessions/minute on the workhorse doors; the doors queue past the OpenCode client's 10s default first-output deadline, every route candidate trips it in the same turn, and the turn ends `failed` with `provider.transport: No response output within 10000ms` — 81 sessions dead in 8h (2026-11-08). Observed first-token maxima already reach ~15.7s on healthy legs.

## Change
`.opencode/opencode.jsonc` set no `health.firstTokenTimeoutMs` on the workhorse chain, so the 10s default applied to every leg. This sets `health: { "firstTokenTimeoutMs": 60000 }` on:
- `workhorse`, `workhorse-ordered`, `workhorse-primary`, `workhorse-weighted` (the chain)
- `deepseek-flash-plan` (the Flash primary pool serving the chain)
- `deepseek-flash` (the plan-only Flash wrapper)

60s is ~4x the observed healthy-leg maximum, sized above the leg p99 under wave queueing, while still bounding a truly dead leg to one minute. ## Evidence

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py` declares no command-line arguments and performs no argument parsing (`main()` takes no parameters, and the script contains no `sys.argv`/`argparse` handling). Unaccounted arguments are ignored and the script proceeds to do its normal read work.

**File:** `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py:1-120,520-551` (module docstring states read-only discovery; `main()` builds/fetches queue, lane-ledger, and OpenCode server state and prints JSON; `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())`).

```bash
python3 -I pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py --bogus
# exits 0 and prints the full JSON discovery payload after performing reads

python3 -I pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py --help
# exits 0 and prints the full JSON discovery payload (no help/usage; work performed)
```

Per `AGENTS.md` ("Operator script argument contract (#3352)") and `doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md`, every operator script must account for its whole command line and parse strictly before any subprocess, network, file write, lock, or deploy step; anything unaccounted for is a usage error with a non-zero exit (2). `poll.py` is a `pm-stack` operator script that reads queue-broker state, lane-ledger state, and OpenCode server session state; ignoring unknown/typo'd flags (including `--help`) means a mis-invocation can silently do real reads instead of failing fast.

body:
Fixes #3179 (queue task 5653).

## Problem
`normalize.sh` built its probe/verify JSON with a regex that stripped only full-line `//` comments. Any inline `//` or `/* */` comment in `opencode.jsonc` made `json.loads` fail, and the script exited 0 with every repair (plugins→plugin, agents→agent) silently skipped.

## Fix
- Replace the regex stripper with a string-aware `jsonc_to_json` scanner in the embedded Python: removes `//` line comments, `/* */` block comments, and trailing commas **only outside string literals** — `//`, `/*`, `,}` and `,]` inside string values are preserved verbatim.
- Used for both the membership probe and the pre-write full-document verification. The repaired output is still spliced from the original text, so comments in the user's file are preserved; normalization semantics outside the JSONC parse path are unchanged.

## Tests
`bash pkgs/opencode-config-normalize/normalize_test.sh` — all 9 cases pass on the laptop worktree:
- 6 pre-existing cases (agents-only, agents-last, merge, plugins-only, unparseable, unrecognised)
- new `inline-comments`, `block-comments`, `string-lookalikes` fixtures asserting the full parsed document and idempotence (the test's `parsed_doc` helper now uses the same string-aware strip)
- The original repro fixtures (inline `//` and block comments over a `plugins` key) went from byte-identical no-op to repaired.

## What

The opencode watchdog (code#7780) treats any serving port as healthy. On 2026-11-10 that blind spot hid the #8255 failure for ~2 days: port 13420 served a two-generations-old build while generation switches reported success, because a service-mode starter silently defers to any registered incumbent.

This PR adds a **build-identity assertion** to the watchdog:

- When `opencode.service` is active, the watchdog reads the registered service's version from `/api/info` (credentials from the channel registration file, never printed) and compares it against the new `services.opencode-watchdog.expectedVersion` option.
- `home/common` sets `expectedVersion` from the name of the very cascade package derivation the unit runs — expectation and ExecStart resolve from one derivation and cannot drift apart (evaluates to `2.0.30+3497ea2` on current main, matching production).
- A mismatch held past the grace window alerts on the same surface as the dark case (the watchdog unit exits 1 until a healthy run) but **never restarts a serving unit**: replacement is the switch procedure's deliberate act, and the watchdog must never race a lifecycle handover.
- Only a positively different reported version counts; an unreadable registration/probe is not evidence. Registration file is channel-selected (`services.opencode-watchdog.channel`, default `prod`). Test hooks: `OPENCODE_WATCHDOG_EXPECTED_VERSION` / `OPENCODE_WATCHDOG_REGISTRATION_FILE`.

- `nix eval` of the host confi

Every live opencode-claimant fire since ~03:02 UTC 2026-11-23 aborts at the cap step: `cap_room` null, `skips: [{reason: cap_unknown}]`, zero sessions launched, supervision skipped. Queue broker is healthy (queue\_health rows present in the fire log); this is not the backend-outage fallback case.

Fire log (`~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/fires.jsonl`):

- `2026-11-23T02:57:23Z` cap\_room 36, 1 candidate (task 20708, #3321), skip sink\_claim\_failed — last good fire
- `2026-11-23T03:02:17Z` cap\_room null, 1 candidate, skip cap\_unknown
- `2026-11-23T03:06:18Z` cap\_room null, 1 candidate, skip cap\_unknown

## Root cause

The primary clone `/home/user/git/code` was checked out from `main` to `xaltha/12751-read-authority` at 2026-11-22 20:55:36 -0600 (reflog), between the last good fire and the first bad one. That branch's `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py` predates the #12225 paging fix: it escalates `GET /api/session?limit=` over (1000, 10000, 100000). The standing OpenCode server (2.0.30+9acf714, pid 1891329, up since 02:26 UTC) caps `limit` at 200 — `?limit=201` and `?limit=1000` both return HTTP 400 `Expected a value less than or equal to 200` (verified repeatedly; auth fine, default list and `/api/session/active` both OK). So `fetch_sessions()` returns None on the first read and the fire fails closed per the cap rule.

`main` already contains the fix (a9542de91c8, `SESSION_FETCH_LIMIT = 200` with cursor paging); the checked-out branch does not. The fail
title: opencode-claimant: all live fires abort at cap since primary clone left on xaltha branch (cap_unknown, nothing launches)

body:
For #3228 (task 8762) — walk-behavior fix. The owner's opendesign credential decision stays open on issue #3228 under user/review; this PR does not close it.

Pool walks in `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs` spent walk attempts on providers whose credential-store row is inactive/missing (`credentialKey()` returns null), and such a leaf's `Authentication` "no credential for provider" error could surface as the run's terminal failure.

## Change
- New `leafCredential`/`hasCredential` helpers (static config `apiKey`, else the active credential-store row); `callLeaf` now uses `leafCredential` (no behavior change there).
- `runCompletion` pre-check: after route resolution + demotion, credential-less candidates are filtered out — skipped exactly like disabled providers. If no credentialed candidate remains, the walk fails with `route <id> has no credentialed members` (tag `UnknownProvider`, retryable 0) **before** any attempt is recorded, so no `route_attempt` is burned and no misleading Authentication error surfaces.

The owner's opendesign credential intent (activate / disable / remove leaves) is untouched — this is walk behavior only, per the task packet's scope exclusion.

## Tests
- `node --test bin/opencode-route-proxy.test.mjs` — **27/27 pass** on the laptop (baseline 25).
- New probe: pool `[leafNoCred (inactive credential row), leafB (healthy)]` completes via leafB with no `route_attempt` against leafNoCred.
- New probe: a walk of only credential-less leaves returns 502 `no cr
title: opencode-route-proxy: skip credential-less leaves in walks (#3228)

body:
## Defect
`send_to_opencode` binds a task to a freshly created session before the prompt is delivered. When the prompt POST times out on the client side (15s), the binding is kept, the session stays empty (zero messages), and the task is stranded until its lease expires and muse-lane re-claims it.

## Evidence
- Task 19897 (#5733): bound 09:40:34Z to `ses_e5e171ed6f4ffepmUsz2TqKooW`; prompt POST returned 499 with span 23708ms at 09:41:00Z; session has zero messages; lease expired 10:25:40Z.
- Task 20151 (#8469): bound 11:16:40Z to `ses_e5e16c6db59ffeg4mIiJTZxndo`; two prompt POSTs 499 (15024ms at 11:16:58Z, 14278ms at 11:17:13Z); zero messages; lease expired 12:02:01Z.
- Fire log (`~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/fires.jsonl`, `kind: send_to_opencode`): of 14 session-creating handoffs since 2026-11-10, 6 have `prompt_ok: false`.
- Counterexample: task 20001 (#6533) prompt POST also returned 499 at 14551ms, but reconcile found messages and `prompt_ok: true`. Reconcile is the only thing separating success from a stranded task.
- Code: `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/send_to_opencode.py` binds (transfer) before prompt (~lines 520-640) with no rollback on prompt failure; `session.create` timeout=15 (line 525); `claimant.py` `_post_prompt` timeout=15 (line 713).
- Related but different: #6533 (handed-off tasks never launched, executed_lane null). #857 in opencode was closed as no-longer-reproducing on a small-prompt test; the cold-session 499 pattern here is a recurrence on a differe
title: send_to_opencode: prompt POST times out on cold session, binding kept on empty session, task stranded

body:
Follow-on from developing-today/opencode#1140 (nested routes conversion).

opencode now treats `experimental.routes.*` as the canonical routing shape (models/providers/windows/schedules/tuning/log/settings) and folds the flat `experimental.model_routes` / `provider_routes` / `model_route_*` keys into it at load via a normalize compat shim. The flat keys remain accepted in the file, so `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs` — which parses the raw JSONC itself and resolves `model_routes` with no shared code — keeps working unchanged today.

Owed work here: teach the proxy to ALSO read `experimental.routes.models` (and `routes.providers`) so a config file written in nested-only form routes correctly through the proxy. The flat shim in opencode must not be removed until this lands (and the OpenChamber validator follow-on lands).

## Acceptance criteria

- `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs` also reads `experimental.routes.models` (and `routes.providers`): a config written in nested-only form routes correctly through the proxy.
- Flat-key configs (`experimental.model_routes` / `provider_routes` / `model_route_*`) route exactly as before.
- Tests cover both shapes, including a mixed config, mirroring the semantics of opencode's normalize compat shim.
- opencode's flat-key shim is NOT removed by this change — removal waits on this and the OpenChamber validator follow-on (developing-today/openchamber issue #1270) both landing.
title: route proxy: learn the nested experimental.routes shape (opencode #1140 follow-on)

body:
## What

Removes the single entry `"@openchamber/opencode-claude@1.3.8"` from the `plugins` array in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`. Nothing else changes (1 line deleted). This file is the global opencode config: `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` is a symlink to it.

## Root cause of the claude-code 404s (opencode#1806)

The stale external plugin `@openchamber/opencode-claude@1.3.8` registers a `session.model.request` hook that rewrites every claude-code provider request baseURL to its own loopback proxy. The native provider then composes `POST http://127.0.0.1:<proxy>/v1/v1/messages`, and the proxy answers with its own plain-text `404 Not Found`. Proven 2026-11-06: removing the plugin restored live Anthropic 200s (PROBEOK on both probe legs, route_attempt outcome success) on fork build 5e9b135f. Both 22c0a6d and 5e9b135f were affected identically — the defect was never in the fork binary, the credential, or the config baseURL; it was this plugin, external to both builds.

## Why this PR is time-critical

Production is already running with this exact edit as an uncommitted working-tree change in the primary checkout (applied as the stopgap through the `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` symlink). The resulting file blob is `885d480582` — byte-identical to this PR branch. Until this lands, any checkout/pull/rebuild that refreshes the working tree resurrects the plugin and re-breaks claude-code; Drew's pending #5647 switch makes that window concrete. This PR makes the production-
title: Remove @openchamber/opencode-claude plugin — root cause of claude-code 404s

body:
Follow-up to the #4544 config split, which found that `opencode-config-normalize` and OpenChamber flap the `plugin`/`agent` keys between v1 and v2 spellings on every OpenChamber launch, and deliberately left the v1 spellings tracked. This fixes the flap at the source: one canonical spelling (v2), everywhere, idempotent.

## Which spelling is canonical, and the evidence

- Every opencode on this machine is the 2.x fork: `opencode --version` = `v2.0.30+6fb3bac` in BOTH the per-user profile and `/run/current-system/sw/bin`. The 1.x CLI — the only consumer that needed v1 (it ignores `plugins` entirely) — is gone.
- The fork source (`packages/core/src/config/normalize.ts`) decodes `input.plugin` via the V1 schema and merges it into `encoded.plugins`; likewise `input.agent`/`input.mode` are migrated into `agents`, with native (v2) entries winning per key (`mergeMaps`).
- Empirically: `opencode debug config` on the live (v1-spelled) file presents the resolved document with `plugins` (13 entries) and `agents` (7) keys.
- OpenChamber already writes native v2 only (`packages/web/server/lib/opencode/config-v2.js` header: "Everything OpenChamber writes is native v2"; `managed-plugin-config.js` folds a legacy `plugin` key into `plugins` and deletes it). **No OpenChamber change is needed** — it was already aligned; normalize was the holdout.

## What changes

- `pkgs/opencode-config-normalize/normalize.sh`: direction flipped. `plugin` -> `plugins` (bare key rename; both present -> legacy-f
title: fix(opencode-config): normalise to canonical v2 plugins/agents keys

body:
Fixes #2533.

## Root cause — the sync was dead for two independent reasons

`syncCodexTokensToOpenCode` in `bin/codex-proxy.mjs` invoked its Python helper as a shell string:

```js
execSync(`python3 -c ${JSON.stringify(script)}`, { stdio: 'ignore' });
```

1. **Quoting:** `JSON.stringify` encodes the script's newlines as literal two-character `\n` sequences. The shell does not expand `\n` inside double quotes, so `python3 -c` received the entire script as one physical line and died instantly with `SyntaxError: unexpected character after line continuation character` — on **every** call, at startup and on the 5-minute interval. Reproduced in isolation with the exact construction against a scratch sqlite DB: same SyntaxError, DB unchanged. `stdio: 'ignore'` discarded the child's stderr and the empty `catch {}` discarded the throw, so the failure was invisible; after a `codex login` the OpenCode store kept stale tokens indefinitely (verified live 2026-10-29; the active `openai` row had to be synced by hand).
2. **No interpreter:** in the deployed service environment there is no `python3` on PATH at all (NixOS: python3 lives in the user profile, which the proxy unit's PATH — `/run/current-system/sw/bin:~/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` — does not include; verified live). Even a correctly quoted child could never have spawned.

## Fix

- The sync now runs **in-process via `node:sqlite`** (`DatabaseSync`, lazily loaded with `createRequire` so a missing module degrades to a logged failure

Adds one scheduled GitHub Actions workflow, `flake-inputs-update`, that keeps the `openchamber` and `opencode` flake inputs current on its own:

- Daily (07:23 UTC, an hour after OpenChamber's own `opencode-update` run lands) plus `workflow_dispatch`.

## Summary

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` is the deterministic fire implementation for the opencode execution lane (slice 1 of #3026). It runs, and its atomic bind/recovery mechanics are correct — but reading it against the packet spec shows several steps are not implemented, and one supervision branch is inverted. All references are to `main` at the time of filing.

Found during the live fire at 2026-11-09T12:22Z while chasing a repeated `bind_failed` skip.

## 1. `candidates_seen` is always `[]` (step 6)

`claimant.py:681` calls `log_fire(mode, [], launched, cap_room, skips)`; the same hardcoded `[]` appears at `:654`, `:663`, `:668`. The fire log's `candidates_seen` field therefore never carries the candidates, so the record cannot answer "what was eligible at this fire" — it only shows launches and skips. Every `fires.jsonl` line to date has `"candidates_seen": []`.

`gate_step()` (`:333`) and `cap_step()` (`:355`) both discard the poll data they fetch.

## 2. No single-instance lock, no bounded pool

The packet describes the fire as launching "distinct candidates in parallel under a bounded pool and a single-instance lock". `launch_step()` (`:427-634`) is a plain sequential `for` loop, and `claimant.py` contains no `fcntl`/`flock`, no thread pool, no `concurrent` import.

Closes #1308. Removes the shadowed duplicate `"cline-pass"` provider block from `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`. Single file, +3/−82 (the +3 is a comment at the surviving block recording the dedup).

## Which block was effective

**The second block** (the one this PR keeps, formerly at line 5124). The fork's config loader — `packages/core/src/config.ts` in developing-today/opencode — parses config with `jsonc-parser`'s `parse()`, which builds a plain object in document order: for a duplicate key, **the later value wins**. The first block (formerly line 4812) was dead config.

## Whether the effective catalog changes

**It does not.** The two blocks turned out to be **byte-identical** — same `npm`/`name`/`options`, same 18 models in the same order with identical entries (verified by direct text diff of the two block bodies, and deep-equality after parsing). So the "union" the issue asks for is just the single 18-model catalog, and nothing was meaningfully shadowed: no model existed only in the dead block.

(Note: the issue said 19 vs 18 entries; the byte-level count on current main is 18 vs 18, matching the "cline-pass 18" figure PR #1304 verified after the sync.)

- Deleted the first (shadowed) block — 82 lines — leaving the effective block in place, per the issue's "place it where the effective block sat".

Every outbound fetch in pm-stack/dispatch except the JWKS one has no timeout or abort signal, so a stalled upstream parks the dispatch handler (and its worker slot) indefinitely — Bun/Node fetch has no default timeout.

Evidence (origin/main 92e96ddaab, read-only):
- pm-stack/dispatch/src/queue.ts:72 (rpc), :115 (patchTask), :145, :195, :224, :259 — bare `await fetch(...)`, no signal.
- pm-stack/dispatch/src/opencode.ts:55 (`api()`) — bare fetch. The catch there maps only connection-refused to a 502 OpenCodeError; a stall never resolves at all.
- pm-stack/dispatch/src/github.ts:147 (`appApi()`) — bare fetch to api.github.com (installation lookup :166, token mint :177).
- Exhaustive: `grep -rn 'AbortSignal|AbortController|timeout' pm-stack/dispatch/src/` returns zero hits.
- Adjacent but distinct: #10738 covers only the JWKS fetch in auth.ts:105 (`fetchGithubJwks`); this issue is the other six call sites. Open-issue search for timeout/fetch-timeout returns #10738 plus unrelated items (#500, #4191, #4191-class in other packages) — no tracker for the Supabase/opencode/GitHub paths; no open PR touches these files for timeouts.

Why it matters: dispatch awaits these inline on the request path. One slow Supabase query, one wedged opencode server, or one api.github.com stall hangs that handler forever; under load this exhausts server concurrency and blocks queue operations fleet-wide. The OIDC path at least fails closed after #10738; these paths hang open with no error at all.

Sugg
title: fix(dispatch): non-JWKS outbound fetches have no timeout — a hung Supabase/opencode/GitHub stalls the handler forever

body:
## Defect

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` read a session's messages from
`GET {OPENCODE_URL}/api/session/<id>/messages` in two places:

- `supervision_step()` — the #4758 "verify zero messages first" guard
  (before deleting a bound session and atomically rebinding its task);
- `_get_messages()` — the reconcile read `_send_prompt()` uses to decide
  whether one resend is allowed.

On the standing laptop OpenCode v2 server that path does not exist: it
returns **HTTP 404 with a zero-byte body**. Both call sites ran curl
*without* `-f` and then `json.loads(stdout or "[]")`, so the 404 parsed
to `[]` — a confirmed "zero messages" that never happened. The correct
endpoint is `GET /api/session/<id>/message`, which returns
`{"data": [ ...messages... ], "cursor": {...}}`.

## Live evidence (2026-11-09, http://127.0.0.1:13420)

Sampled four real sessions from `GET /api/session`:

```
ses_e5e40adbccfffe5tL3Wrx51oUl  /messages 404 (0 bytes)  /message 200  n=100 at limit=100
ses_e5e403fe19cffeWYfpPV90r6Ta  /messages 404 (0 bytes)  /message 200  n=58
ses_e5e3fbfb4a1ffeHj2ReQt5sy1v  /messages 404 (0 bytes)  /message 200  n=17
ses_e5e403fe514ffeSDLSefGjZqEF  /messages 404 (0 bytes)  /message 200  n=89
```

The default page is 20 messages; `?limit=100` returns the counts above,
confirming `/message` really carries the full list. (The task report
encountered 29 and 25 messages for two other sessions; the point is the
same: `/messages` 404s, `/message` 200s with `{"data": [...]}`.)
title: fix(opencode-claimant): read session messages from /message and fail closed on unknown

The both-present `plugin`+`plugins` merge re-serialised the merged array with `json.dumps`, silently deleting every comment inside both arrays while exiting 0. The pre-write verification compared comment-stripped parses, so the loss verified as correct.

The opencode execution lane has never bound a handed-off task through claimant.py: lanes hand off, the claimant fires, and nothing launches. Four defects compounded:

- poll.py json-parsed the repo-queue binary's list output, which is a human table since the #5362 cutover, so every queue read as empty and the gate always exited (#7325, #7375).
- The checkpoint verb records the yield at progress.last_checkpoint.stage; is_candidate reads progress.stage, so even a working read classified ~0 candidates (#7706).
- launch_step never read mode — a shadow fire reaching step 4 would have created and bound sessions (#7366) — and it bound sessions without ever sending the execution prompt, manufacturing #4758 zero-message sessions (#7356). Its session calls also carried none of the server's required Basic auth.
- The broker's rich /list (built for this claimant) did not return the task payload, so launch prompts carried an empty packet.

Fixes:

- poll.py reads claimed rows from the broker's /list with rich: true (URL/token resolved exactly as the fleet client resolves them), lifts the yield stage from last_checkpoint, and exposes payload as the candidate packet. Fail-closed semantics unchanged: an unreadable queue contributes no rows.
- claimant.py supervision reads rows through poll.py; launch_step in shadow mode records the would-launch window as skips and mutates nothing; the live launch creates the session with auth, binds it, then delivers the prompt via POST /api/session/{id}/pro
title: fix(opencode-claimant): make handed-off tasks actually bind and execute (task 13488)

New pm-stack service `pm-dispatch` (Drew's request, 2026-10-30): an HTTP service on the laptop with two authenticated endpoints.

- `POST /v1/sessions` — launch an OpenCode session on the laptop immediately: creates a GitHub issue (optional, default on), enqueues a repo-health queue task, launches the session with the prompt, and marks the task claimed immediately (worker `dispatch-opencode`, session id in progress) so no lane double-books it.
- `POST /v1/tasks` — enqueue-only: puts a repo-task/v1 packet into the Supabase queue (repo-health-*-pilot), optionally with a GitHub issue.
- Auth: GitHub Actions OIDC (aud `pm-dispatch`, token's repository claim must equal the request's repo) or a static bearer secret.
- `GET /health` unauthenticated, aggregator-style build version.

Deployed on the laptop like the aggregator (install.sh + user systemd unit, loopback + tailnet bind). Public reachability (a Cloudflare tunnel hostname on amd-6-pm-stack) is a separate later step.

**Defect: opencode.service first-start deadlock — `EnvironmentFile` is loaded before the `ExecStartPre` materializer that creates it can run.**

Found during the 2026-11-04 evening switch re-run (the first switch to land the unit in this shape). The deployed unit carries:

```
EnvironmentFile=%h/.local/state/opencode/mistral-api-key.env
ExecStartPre=/nix/store/…-opencode-mistral-key-materialize
```

The materializer creates `mistral-api-key.env` (umask 077, writes `MISTRAL_API_KEY=…`). But when the file is absent, systemd fails the start before the materializer can ever run:

```
opencode.service: Failed to load environment files: No such file or directory
opencode.service: Failed to spawn 'start-pre' task: No such file or directory
opencode.service: Failed with result 'resources'.
… restart counter climbs … Failed with result 'start-limit-hit'.
```

The old server was stopped at activation (21:15:40 CST) and the service stayed down until the materializer was run once by hand, after which `reset-failed` + `start` brought it up clean and the façade verified (401 unauth / 200 authenticated route completion). So the end state is recoverable, but any start from a state where the env file is missing — state-dir cleanup, first deploy, a future activation that prunes it — deadlocks the same way.

**Fix directions (any one):**
- Prefix the EnvironmentFile path with `-` (optional load) so the first start can run the materializer, which creates the file for the ExecStart spawn; or
- Mo

## What

`pm-stack/dispatch/src/opencode.ts`: both JSON parses in the OpenCode client are now boundary validations in the module's own vocabulary.

Fixes #6915.

`readState` in `pm-stack/opencode-usage-export/opencode-usage-export.mjs` returned `JSON.parse(state.json)` verbatim, and `run()` dereferenced `state.storePath` unchecked:

- `state.json` containing the JSON literal `null` made every tick throw a raw `TypeError`, exit 6 as `read-failed`, and overwrite the last good `latest.json` with a failure document — self-perpetuating, since the failure path never rewrites `state.json`, and misdiagnosed as a store read failure while the store was fresh.

The tick then proceeds normally and rewrites `state.json` in the correct shape, so a wrong-shape state file self-heals.

body:
Fixes #6939 (task 11326).

## What
`parseServerUrl` in `bin/opencode-acp-adapter.mjs` took the `--server` value unchecked: a trailing `--server` was silently dropped (adapter dialled the default serve), `--server=` set an empty base that looped forever on `Failed to parse URL`, a flag-like value was consumed verbatim as the URL, and a typo'd flag was silently ignored.

Following the sibling strict-argv pattern from #3449 (provider-catalog-sync):
- `--server` with a missing (trailing), empty, or flag-like value fails fast at startup with a usage error naming the flag and the offending value (exit 2), before the event stream starts.
- A value that is not a parseable `http:`/`https:` URL (or has no host) fails the same way; the resolved `OPENCODE_ACP_SERVER` env value is validated too.
- Unknown arguments (e.g. the `--sever` typo) are rejected with a usage error naming the argument — per the #3352 contract, a typo can no longer silently change which server is dialled.
- Valid forms unchanged: `--server <url>`, `--server=<url>`, trailing-slash stripping, `OPENCODE_ACP_SERVER` env fallback, built-in default.

## Tests
New spawn-level regression tests in `bin/opencode-acp-adapter.test.mjs` cover trailing `--server`, `--server=`, flag-like value, non-URL value, non-http(s) value, and the typo'd-flag case — each asserting a fast exit 2 naming `--server`.

`node --test bin/opencode-acp-adapter.test.mjs` — 16 passed, 0 failed (10 existing + 6 new), run on the laptop worktree at 394b0d2

body:
## Symptom

The opencode-claimant packet mandates `--worker opencode-claimant` on **every** `repo-queue` verb it uses. The deployed binary rejects that flag on two of the verbs the claimant's read path depends on:

```
$ repo-queue health --queue repo-health-code-pilot --worker opencode-claimant
repo-queue: unrecognized argument: --worker

$ repo-queue list --queue repo-health-code-pilot --status claimed --worker opencode-claimant
repo-queue: unrecognized argument: --worker
```

Verbs that accept it (probed 2026-11-08): `bind`, `checkpoint`, `heartbeat`, `claim`, `fail`, `complete`, `park`, `block`, `lane`.
Verbs that reject it: `list`, `health`.

## Impact

- `poll.py`'s `fetch_claimed_rows()` does **not** pass `--worker`, so it is unaffected today — but any attempt to bring the read path into line with the packet (as #7325's fix will touch) fails at the CLI.
- The packet's own contract ("pass `--worker opencode-claimant` on every verb you use") is unsatisfiable as written for the read verbs, so a fire that follows the packet literally aborts on its first `health` call.
- Note the failure mode is at least loud (`unrecognized argument`) rather than silently ignored — unlike #3278.

## Proposed fix

Either accept (and ignore, or use for attribution) `--worker` on `list` and `health`, or amend the claimant packet to scope `--worker` to the mutating verbs only. The former keeps the packet uniform and matches every other verb.

## What broke

`workhorse` attempts on `antigravity-direct/claude-sonnet-5-5` 400'd on a ~30-minute cadence all day 2026-11-03 (route ledger 17:34 / 18:04 / 18:34 / 19:34Z). Upstream error, Anthropic-shaped:

    tools.9.custom.input_schema: JSON schema is invalid. It must match JSON Schema draft 2020-12 (https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12).

Tracked as developing-today/opencode#1550. This is the door half of the fix; the fork twin lands in developing-today/opencode (same title).

## Root cause (probed live against the door, 2026-11-03)

For Claude models the upstream re-serializes the v1internal proto Schema into an Anthropic `input_schema` — and Anthropic's validator rejects **`anyOf` outright**: any branch count (even one), any position (root, property, nested in `items`). Every other probed shape passes on the Claude leaf: no tools, minimal tools, bare array properties, type-array null unions (the converter collapses those to `nullable`), `additionalProperties`, inlined `$ref`s, `oneOf` (2- and 3-branch, object branches), `allOf`. Gemini models accept `anyOf` verbatim. Any real tool whose zod schema carries a union (`.nullable()`, type unions) therefore 400s every Claude attempt while Gemini sails through.

## Fix

At the translation boundary only: `convertSchema`/`convertSchemaNode` take an `anthropic` flag (from `buildV1Request`: the resolved base model starts with `claude`), and for Anthropic targets `anyOf` is emitted as `oneOf`, recursively (properties, items, pre
title: fix(antigravity-direct): fold anyOf to oneOf for Claude targets (opencode#1550)

body:
## What
`convertSchemaNode` in `bin/antigravity-direct.mjs` now synthesizes an unconstrained `items: {}` whenever the converted schema type is `ARRAY` and neither `items` nor `prefixItems` is present.

## Why (developing-today/opencode#1548)
A tool property declared `{type: "array"}` with no `items` is legal JSON Schema (unconstrained elements), but the Cloud Code v1internal proto validator rejects an ARRAY schema carrying neither field:

    GenerateContentRequest.tools[0].function_declarations[17].parameters.properties[paths].items: missing field

The converter only synthesized `items` for the tuple/`prefixItems` case, so any tool with a bare array property 400'd every tool-carrying session through the door. Reproduced live against the running door before the fix (single tool, `paths: {type: "array"}` -> upstream 400 with the exact message above; same tool with `items` -> 200).

The fork's twin converter (`packages/ai/src/protocols/antigravity.ts`, ported from this file) has the identical flaw and gets the identical fix in a companion opencode PR, so the in-fork provider does not reintroduce this when it deploys.

## Tests
`node --test bin/antigravity-direct.test.mjs` — 17/17 pass, including a new case asserting the converted upstream payload for the exact failing shape plus nested/anyOf/tuple positions and an invariant sweep (no ARRAY node without items/prefixItems).

Deploy note: the unit execs this file from the primary checkout, so merge + primary sync + `systemctl --us
title: fix(antigravity-direct): synthesize items for bare array tool schemas (opencode#1548)
