body:
## Problem

`pkgs/opencode-config-normalize/normalize.sh` silently performs **no repair at all** on an `opencode.jsonc` that contains an inline `//` comment or a `/* */` block comment — the two comment forms JSONC allows anywhere, and the forms a hand-edited user config most often contains. The config keeps its v2 `plugins`/`agents` keys, which opencode 1.x ignores (the script's own header documents this), so the user's plugins/agents stay broken while the path-unit trigger reports nothing.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `fc88d0a9`, script sha256 `c59dd79b…`)

- `normalize.sh:36-41`: the membership probe strips only full-line comments — `re.sub(r'^\s*//.*$', '', raw, flags=re.M)` — then `json.loads(probe)`; on any exception it does `sys.exit(0)` ("unparseable: leave it alone"). An inline comment after a value, or a `/* */` block, is not stripped, so the parse fails and the script exits 0 having changed nothing. The same weak probe is reused for the pre-write verification at lines 108-109.
- Laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneA-normalize/`, verbatim copy of the script, sha-matched to main):
  - Case A: config with `"plugins": ["opencode-plugin-x"] // migrated by OpenChamber` → exit 0, file byte-identical, `plugins` still present.
  - Case A2: config with a `/* user config */` header comment and `"plugins": [...]` → exit 0, file byte-identical, `plugins` still present.
  - Control case B (no comments) repairs correctly, proving the fixtures are otherwise in
title: opencode-config-normalize: an inline // or /* */ comment anywhere in opencode.jsonc silently disables every repair — the probe stripper only removes full-line comments, the parse fails, and the script exits 0

## What

Comment-only change to `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` (verified: every changed line is a `//` comment; the file still parses as JSONC). No window, route, target, or any other config value changes.

## Why

DeepSeek's peak/off-peak rules were re-verified on 2026-10-29 against DeepSeek's own pricing page (https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing/), footnote (2), verbatim:

> "(2) Off-peak rates are half of the peak rates. Peak hours are 01:00 - 04:00 and 06:00 - 10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. All other hours are off-peak, including weekends and Chinese public holidays in full."

Reconciliation against the shipped windows:

- **Peak times — RIGHT.** `deepseek-peak-early` Mon–Fri 01:00–04:00 UTC and `deepseek-peak-late` Mon–Fri 06:00–10:00 UTC match the official windows exactly.
- **Weekends — RIGHT.** The windows are Mon–Fri only, so weekends are off-peak in full, exactly as specified. Chinese make-up workdays that fall on a weekend do **not** become peak under the official text, and the config correctly does not treat them as peak.
- **Chinese public holidays — NOT ENCODED (the gap this PR documents).** A holiday falling Mon–Fri is off-peak for the whole day, but the shipped windows still treat it as peak. Weekday examples from the official 2026 PRC State Council arrangement: National Day Thu Oct 1, Fri Oct 2, Mon Oct 5 – Wed Oct 7, 2026 were all off-peak in full and were routed as peak.

The gap is a schema limitation, not a

Fixes #4758

Phase 3 of design #4912 (claimant session contract): a bound session that never received its prompt previously had no recovery path — not a launch candidate, resend already spent, gone-session rule inapplicable while the empty session existed.

**poll.py (read-only discovery)**
- New `stuck_bound` output (top-level + per-queue): claimed opencode-lane tasks bound to a root session with no terminal marker (`time.idle`/`outcome`), NOT in the server's active set, silent for at least `ACTIVE_WINDOW_MS` (the existing 30-minute zombie window — one threshold, not two), and with the task's lease expired. Every unknown fails closed (unreadable active set, missing session, unparseable lease all veto). Entries carry `attempts`/`max_attempts` so the claimant can pick the branch. Zero-message verification is deliberately NOT claimed from the session list — the claimant must verify it before acting.
- `is_candidate` now accepts stage `launch_failed` alongside `handed_off` as a recorded yield, so a task reclaimed by the recovery rule becomes a launch candidate again instead of being stranded by its own recovery checkpoint.

**prompt.md (claimant contract)**
- Step 1 gains the recovery rule: verify zero messages (any message/marker/activity vetoes — a live, progressing session is never reclaimed) → DELETE the verified zero-message session per-id FIRST (a failed or unverifiable delete keeps the binding, fail closed) → attempts remain: checkpoint `launch_failed` as the task's worke

## What

New pm-stack service **pm-dispatch** (`pm-stack/dispatch/`), per Drew's 2026-10-30 request: an authenticated HTTP service on the laptop that ferries prompts to the laptop's OpenCode server and/or into the Supabase repo-health queues — always tracked, never fire-and-forget.

- **`POST /v1/sessions` — launch now.** Creates the tracking GitHub issue (default on), enqueues a repo-task/v1 queue task, creates an OpenCode session on the standing laptop server (127.0.0.1:13420) in the repo's primary directory with the requested model, sends the prompt (prefixed with the task/issue/repo ids), and marks the task **claimed immediately** (`worker_id: dispatch-opencode`, session id in `progress`) so no queue worker double-books it. `wait:false` answers `202` after the enqueue and finishes the launch asynchronously; a failed launch cancels the task and notes the issue.
- **`POST /v1/tasks` — enqueue only.** Same packet machinery (kind, priority incl. name mapping, model hint, optional issue, canonical or caller-supplied dedupe keys) without launching a session.
- **`GET /health`** — unauthenticated `{ok, version}`, aggregator-style.

## Auth

- **GitHub Actions OIDC**: RS256 verified against GitHub's JWKS (cached), `aud: pm-dispatch`; the token's `repository` claim must be allowlisted **and equal the request body's repo** — a workflow can only dispatch for its own repo.
- **Static bearer secret** (`DISPATCH_API_TOKEN`), constant-time compared — the shape a repo stores as an Action
title: feat(pm-stack): pm-dispatch — launch/track OpenCode sessions from GitHub Actions

body:
## Symptom

Every `claimant.py` fire that ends at the gate writes a **false** `cap_room: 0` into the fire log:

```
{"timestamp": "2026-11-08T14:20:19Z", "mode": "shadow", "candidates_seen": [], "sessions_launched": [], "cap_room": 0, "skips": [{"reason": "no_candidates"}]}
```

But `poll.py`, run seconds later against the same server, reports real headroom:

```
cap: 36  concurrency_cap: 36  live_root: 9094  active_root: 4  cap_room: 32
```

## Cause

`claimant.py:533` hardcodes `0` in the gate-exit path:

```python
if not has_candidates:
    print("No unbound opencode-lane candidates found. Exiting.")
    log_fire(mode, [], [], 0, [{"reason": "no_candidates"}])
    return 0
```

`cap_step()` is never reached — it runs *after* the gate — so the value logged is a placeholder, not a measurement.

## Why it matters

`cap_room` in `fires.jsonl` is the field an operator reads to answer "was this fire idle because the fleet was full, or because nothing was eligible?" With the gate-exit path writing `0`, every candidate-less fire is indistinguishable from a saturated one.

This is not hypothetical confusion: the fire log shows `cap_room: 0` for the 14:05, 14:10, 14:15 and 14:20 fires on 2026-11-08 while the true cap_room was ~31-32. A reader would conclude the fleet was pinned at the 36 cap; it was at 4 active roots.

It also masks #7325. A blind-discovery fire and a genuinely-empty-queue fire both log `no_candidates` with `cap_room: 0`, so the log cannot distinguish "nothing to do
title: opencode-claimant(claimant.py): gate-exit logs a hardcoded cap_room 0 — idle fires read as cap-saturated

body:
## Root cause

The `vibe-direct` provider entry in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` declared `"limit": { "context": 262144 }` on `mistral-vibe-cli-latest`. The fork's v1 provider schema (`ConfigProviderV1.Model.limit`) requires `output` alongside `context`, and config normalization drops an entry **whole** when it fails schema decode (`skipped malformed recognized value` at `$.provider.vibe-direct`).

So after the 2026-11-04 switch, the provider never entered the catalog under any id — `/api/provider/vibe-direct` and `/api/provider/vibe` both 404 — and the `mistral-plan` provider route logged `member "vibe-direct" names no known provider; it contributes no leaves` 5,096 times.

Ruled out with evidence:
- **Stale build**: the running server is `opencode-2.0.30+7774bf0`, and `7774bf0` is opencode#1661's merge commit itself — the vibe provider code is in the build.
- **Credential gating**: with the fixed entry, the provider registers `activation: enabled` with no credential resolvable (no env key, no `~/.vibe/.env`, keyring `ai.mistral.vibe` absent). Registration is not gated on sign-in.

## Fix

Remove the malformed `limit` block (the verified context 262144 already rides in the provider's own preset, opencode#1661 `vibe.ts` MODELS, and reaches the runtime model from there — verified `limit.context: 262144` on the live model), and replace the comment with the schema gotcha so the next editor doesn't re-add a context-only limit.

## Verification (deployed binary, standalone)

- Fixed
title: fix(opencode-config): drop malformed limit that kept vibe-direct out of the catalog

From the placement-framework v1 synthesis on #2024 (design doc PR linked there); the registry requirement was first specified in the #2020 Jules investigation.

## What
One fleet-side schedule registry covering ALL THREE schedule surfaces, as a single committable record:

- **Muse cron** — judgement-bearing fleet jobs
- **OpenCode schedules** — OS timer + `opencode run` units (#2019 pattern; implementation #2232)
- **Jules schedules** — web-UI CRUD on the one collected account (pilot #2265)

Per schedule: surface, name/id, repo/scope, cadence, route or pool, prompt/brief pointer (verbatim for Jules), budget expectation, owner, kill criteria, date created, last review.

## Why
Each surface's native UI/state is invisible to the other two. Without one registry, schedules are invisible to fleet reviews — the failure mode #2020 named — and the placement framework's "which surface owns this recurring work" question cannot be answered from evidence.

## Acceptance
- Registry file created and populated for all currently-known schedules on the three surfaces (Jules section may start with the #2265 pilot entry + an explicit "none others known" note).
- Creating/retiring a schedule on any surface updates the registry in the same pass (written into the relevant job/runbook text).

body:
### What happened

After the opencode server lifecycle change (T3 now spawns its own managed `opencode serve` on demand, on a random port, instead of reusing a long-lived server on :4096), the OpenCode provider card in the app shows:

```
OpenCode 2 is running, but it did not list any models yet.
```

and every opencode model in the picker shows **Unavailable**. The state never recovers on its own.

### Root cause (verified with live debugging on a 3-box fleet)

1. T3 spawns the managed serve and probes the model list **once, immediately after the port binds** (probe timestamp == spawn timestamp in `userdata/caches/opencode.json`).
2. opencode 2.2.5 (official `@opencode/cli`, published 2026-10-30) needs **~60s** from port-bind until `/api/model` starts answering. During that window it returns:
   ```json
   {"_tag":"ServiceUnavailableError","message":"Location plugins did not finish activating","service":"plugin"}
   ```
3. The spawn-time probe always lands inside that window, so T3 caches `status: "warning", models: []` and **never re-probes** (`checkedAt` stays frozen; no retry, no probe on app-open, no probe on later sessions).
4. Sessions themselves work fine (turns complete normally on opencode models) - only the cached provider state is poisoned, so the picker stays Unavailable indefinitely.

Ruled out as causes (A/B tested): custom user plugins (removed - same 503), MCP servers (disabled - same 503), minimal single-provider config (same 503), serve cwd (same 503). The
title: OpenCode picker stuck Unavailable: provider probe races model activation (fires once at serve spawn, never retries)

Implementation slice scoped by triage task 8950 (lane W, 2026-11-04) extending #3325 leg-shedding to the #4370 death classes. Findings and full evidence are on #3325 (task 8950 comment) and #4370.

## Problem (verified at main, blob 70f01618, bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs, 1095 lines)

- `callLeaf`'s fetch passes only the shared walk signal — there is no per-leg timeout. A hung/slow leg holds the walk; the only cap is the whole-walk `TIMEOUT_MS` (line 62, default 1,200,000 ms).
- `runCompletion` does fall through on per-leaf transport errors, but only while the signal is not aborted; the OpenCode client's ~10 s no-output window (`provider.transport` "No response output within 10000ms", #4370) kills the session first, and a client abort is terminal in the walk.
- Net effect: a transport-timeout leg is never shed in time — ~30 fleet sessions died this way on 2026-11-01 (#4370).

- Per-leaf first-response (headers) timeout in `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs`, configurable via env in the existing `OPENCODE_ROUTE_PROXY_*` pattern, sized well under the client no-output window; on timeout, record the attempt (outcome `timeout`, tag `Transport`, `failedOverTo` set) and continue the walk.
- Proxy tests: hung first leg sheds to a live second leg inside the timeout; ledger row written.

# opencode-acp-adapter: a JSON `null` line on stdin crashes the adapter — dispatch destructures the parsed message unguarded

## Summary

`bin/opencode-acp-adapter.mjs` (the ACP-to-HTTP adapter, #1243) reads newline-delimited JSON-RPC from stdin. A line that is not valid JSON is handled: it is logged and ignored. But a line that is valid JSON with the value `null` kills the whole adapter process — every in-flight session the client (OpenClaw acpx) is driving through it dies with it, and no error is ever returned on the protocol channel.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop @ 84890c3667)

The readline handler parses the line and calls `dispatch` without checking the parsed value is an object:

- `bin/opencode-acp-adapter.mjs:554-559` — `message = JSON.parse(trimmed)` (only the parse is inside try/catch), then `void dispatch(message);`
- `bin/opencode-acp-adapter.mjs:520` — `async function dispatch(message) { const { id, method, params } = message; … }`

Destructuring `null` throws, `dispatch` is `void`-called, so the throw becomes an unhandled rejection and Node exits.

- Control — `initialize` request alone: correct response, process alive.

  ```

## Problem

Two fire-log gaps in `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` make a fire's outcome
impossible to reconstruct after the fact. Both were hit live on 2026-11-09.

### 1. A failed queue read is logged as "no candidates"

`gate_step()` runs `poll.py` and looks at `candidates`. `poll.fetch_claimed_rows()`
returns `[]` on any broker failure (it prints a warning to stderr). `run_poll()`
captures stderr and only checks the exit code, so a transient broker read failure is
indistinguishable from a genuinely empty queue, and the fire logs:

```json
{"reason": "no_candidates"}
```

Observed: the 12:17:51Z fire logged `no_candidates` while `poll.py` run minutes
before and after returned four `handed_off` candidates for the same queue
(`13723`, `13748`, `13813`, `14120`). Nothing launched either way (cap_room was 0),
but the log states a fact that was not established.

### 2. `bind_failed` discards the error, so a repeat failure is undiagnosable

In `launch_step()` a failed bind deletes the freshly created session and records
only `{"reason": "bind_failed"}`. `bind_result.stderr` — which is where
`bind_repo_task_lane_session` says exactly which precondition failed (task not
claimed with a live lease / no lane ledger row / already bound to session X /
task does not exist) — is dropped.

Observed: task `8750` hit `bind_failed` at the 10:06:00Z fire **and** again at the
12:29:18Z fire. Each attempt created and deleted a session, and the log cannot say
whether the lease had lapsed,
title: opencode-claimant: fire log cannot distinguish a failed queue read from an empty queue, or say why a bind failed

## What

`bin/opencode-acp-adapter.mjs` — a single-purpose Node executable following the bin/*.mjs pattern that speaks ACP (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, newline-delimited) on one side and the OpenCode serve HTTP API on the other, targeting the standing shared server (default `http://127.0.0.1:13420`, `--server` flag / `OPENCODE_ACP_SERVER` env; `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` sent as basic auth when set). ## Problem

`bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs` parses its per-request deadline with a bare `Number()`:

- `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs:51` — `const TIMEOUT_MS = Number(process.env.OPENCODE_ROUTE_PROXY_TIMEOUT_MS || 1_200_000);`
- `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs:535-538` — the value goes straight into `setTimeout(() => deadlineCtl.abort(...), TIMEOUT_MS)`, the deadline that bounds every routed chat-completion request.

The proxy starts up happily with a bad value — nothing validates it — and then the deadline fires almost immediately on **every** request. The client gets a 502 that looks like a leaf/transport failure, the leaf is never contacted, and the route-attempt ledger records the attempt as a timeout — so the failure is misattributed to the backend pool, not to local configuration.

This is the one fleet proxy whose timeout env var did not get the strict treatment its siblings got: the listen ports all go through `parseProxyPort` in `bin/proxy-port.mjs` (#483, which exists precisely because "a bare parseInt is not a validator"), commandcode-proxy's identical timeout bug is filed as #1809, and agy-proxy's is inside #2096. The route proxy's was missed.

## Part 2 of the opencode#1550 fix (the schema half was #5110)

Live verification of #5110 caught a second, distinct Claude-leaf 400 in the route ledger minutes after deploy: a `workhorse` session succeeded on the leaf at 20:20:02Z, then its next step 400'd at 20:20:18Z with a different Anthropic error:

    messages.1.content.0.tool_use.id: Field required

## Root cause (reproduced + probed live)

Any request whose **history** contains an assistant tool call 400s on the Claude leaf. The door converted OpenAI tool calls to v1internal `functionCall` parts with no id (Gemini pairs calls by name/order and never needed one). For Claude models the upstream's v1internal→Anthropic conversion emits one `tool_use` block per `functionCall` part — with no id — and Anthropic rejects it. Adding the id to `functionCall` moved the error to the result side (`tool_result.tool_use_id: Field required`), confirming the proto's `id` field on both part kinds is the interop channel.

Probed against a scratch instance of this door on the real upstream before merging: history with a single call, parallel calls, two full tool rounds, and streaming — all 400 before, all **200** after. First turns were never affected; every continuation was.

## Fix

For Claude targets only (`anthropic` flag from part 1):
- history `functionCall` parts carry the client's `tool_call` id; `functionResponse` parts carry the matching `tool_call_id`.
- Response side: an upstream-provided call id is kept when one arrives (Ant

Fixes #2364 · queue task 4335

## The bug
`normalize.sh` folded `agents` into `agent` by splicing the merged map into an existing `"agent"` block, then dropped the `agents` block **unconditionally**. For an agents-only config — exactly the shape OpenChamber's v1→v2 migration produces — the splice regex could never match, so nothing was inserted, the `agents` block was deleted anyway, and the script reported "repaired" with exit 0 while every agent definition vanished.

Reproduced on main `bd1379847`: agents-only fixture (`build` + `plan`, plus `plugins`) came out as just `{ "$schema": …, "plugin": ["opencode-plugin-x"] }`.

## The fix
- **Insert path:** when there is no `agent` block, the `agents` block itself is replaced with the merged `agent` block (trailing comma preserved), so the fold is atomic in one substitution.
- **Verify-before-drop:** the result is written only when its full parsed document equals the intended document (`doc` with `plugins`→`plugin` applied and `agents` folded into `agent`, existing `agent` winning per key). Any splice/insert/verify failure exits 1 with the file left byte-identical — pinned convention: a repair tool is never a data-loss path.
- The plugins→plugin rename and the unparseable-input behaviour (exit 0, untouched) are unchanged.

## Tests
New `pkgs/opencode-config-normalize/normalize_test.sh` — the package's first test file. Six fixtures, each asserting the **full parsed document** plus idempotence (second run byte-identical no-op):

Fixes #4770.

## What
`delete_top_level_entry` in `normalize.sh` located a preceding block comment with a plain backward `rfind('/*')`, which selects an inner literal `/*` inside the comment body (e.g. `/* example syntax: /* text */`) instead of the real opening delimiter. The scan then failed closed with exit 1 on a previously supported commented layout before a final legacy `agent` entry.

## Change
- `normalize.sh`: new `_block_comment_start_ending_at` helper — a forward lexical scan (string- and //-aware) finds the comment closing exactly at the scan point. Replaces the `rfind` in the last-entry separator loop.
- `normalize_test.sh`: regression case 24 (inner-`/*` block comment before final `agent`, comment text asserted byte-identical), and the failure-count gate moved to the end of the file so every case — including the previously ungated comment-before-agent-last case — affects the suite exit status.

- Reproduced on origin/main \Μ΅f1577891e: fixture exits 1, file byte-identical.

body:
Follow-up to #6157, found by its live verification: sessions pinned to `opencode-route/deepseek-flash-plan#low` and `#high` failed with `Variant unavailable`.

**Mechanism:** a route offers only variants every target can produce natively or via remap (`routeVariants` = intersection; model-resolver.ts). `mistral-plan/mistral-small-latest` produced no named variant: the provider-route group's variant set is the intersection of its legs, and vibe-direct's hand-declared catalog entry for mistral-small-latest carried **no variants at all**, emptying the group — and with it the pool's whole variant set. (Unpinned sessions were unaffected; parents like workhorse would have silently dropped the pool leg at pinned variants.)

**Fix (config only):**
- Declare the attested variants on vibe-direct's `mistral-small-latest`: `none`/`high` reasoning effort — the same variants the models.dev-backed `mistral` provider catalog carries for this model id on the same Mistral wire.
- Remap the pool's rungs on the mistral-plan target: `low→none`, `medium/high/xhigh/max→high`. Both values are producible by both of mistral-plan's legs, so its plan leg (vibe-direct, ordered first inside the group) stays in front at every rung.

mistral-plan's own definition is untouched. Deploy = merge + primary pull + opencode.service restart, then the probe battery re-runs.

Claim-time execution-lane assignment for the repo queues:

Adds the `luna-haiku-100k` pool: Haiku #high + Luna #xhigh behind the route context cap from developing-today/opencode#554 (merged), so sessions pinned to this pool compact at 100k context — inside the much cheaper sub-100k pricing tier both models have.

## The pool

- `haiku-plan#high` — AA intelligence 38 at this rung, fast (~175+ t/s class), plan pool.
- `luna-plan#xhigh` — AA intelligence 35, ~126 t/s output; time-to-first-token 24.2s at xhigh (vs 93.8s at max, AA's current published figures).
- `limit.context: 100000` — the route presents a 100k context limit regardless of the targets' own (much larger) limits, so compaction and context accounting keep sessions under the cliff.

## Safety on current serves

The cap field is new in the fork. On fork builds predating opencode#554 the config decoder silently strips the unknown `limit` key from routes (verified against the pre-#554 schema: decode succeeds, field dropped), so this config is harmless before the fork deploys and takes effect automatically once a serve runs a build with #554. Until then the pool resolves as an ordinary uncapped Haiku+Luna pool.

Nothing else changes: no agent re-pointed at the pool, no existing pool touched. Sessions opt in by pinning to `luna-haiku-100k`.

## Defect

The route proxy resolves the plan-backed GPT providers (`openai`, `openai.alternate`) to the wrong backend door.

code#3256 recorded that both provider blocks in the deployed config are empty shells. OpenCode tolerates that because its built-in `openai` provider wires the ACTIVE credential to its proper backend: `chatgpt-browser` (main) and `chatgpt-headless` (alternate) both talk to the ChatGPT/Codex backend, not to `api.openai.com`.

code PR #3830 closed the proxy symptom by adding built-in endpoint defaults in `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs`, including `https://api.openai.com/v1` for `openai`. That is the PAYG platform door. Live proof on 2026-11-02 (see code#2518 evidence: https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/2518#issuecomment-6581998868) showed both GPT members answering 429 through the proxy, with the main leaf reporting "no credits remaining" from the platform door, while the fork's internal routing to the same plans works.

## Required fix

The proxy must resolve a leaf provider the way OpenCode itself resolves it: provider + its active credential determines the backend. No invented vendor defaults.

- Configured `baseURL` wins when present.
- Otherwise use built-in resolution keyed by the provider's ACTIVE credential type: `chatgpt-browser` / `chatgpt-headless` -> ChatGPT/Codex backend using the fork's exact request contract; a genuine platform/API-key credential -> platform door.
- Remove the `api.openai.com` default for plan-backed providers.

title: opencode-route-proxy: GPT providers resolved to api.openai.com (PAYG door) instead of the credential-backed Codex backend

body:
## Problem

`mcpx stats` grouped opencode statistics always report `messages: 0`, even for sessions that have messages.

This is the same defect as dezren39/nix#393 (fixed there by dezren39/nix PR #394), present in this repo's `pkgs/mcpx` copy and not fixed here. Verified on main (54c223ce): this repo's `pkgs/mcpx/internal/opencode/opencode.go` is byte-identical to the pre-fix version in dezren39/nix.

## Evidence

- `pkgs/mcpx/internal/opencode/opencode.go:175-182` — `Group` declares `Messages int64 \`json:"messages"\``.
- `pkgs/mcpx/internal/opencode/opencode.go:214` — `ByModel` merges groups with `m.Messages += g.Messages`, so the field is expected to be populated.
- `pkgs/mcpx/internal/opencode/opencode.go:259-287` — `group()` (used by `ByAgent`, `ByModel`, `ByProject`) builds `SELECT %s AS k, count(*), %s, %s, %s FROM session ...` (key, session count, cost, tokens in, tokens out — no message count) and scans only `&g.Key, &g.Sessions, &g.Cost, &g.TokensIn, &g.TokensOut`. `Group.Messages` is therefore never populated and always serializes as `0`.
- There is no test file at all in `pkgs/mcpx/internal/opencode/` in this repo, so nothing catches it.
- Contrast: `Busiest` in the same file does count messages per session with a correlated subquery on `message.session_id`, which is the pattern the fix should reuse.

## Why it matters

Anyone reading grouped stats (by agent / model / project) from this repo's mcpx gets a permanently-zero message count — a silently wrong number,
title: mcpx stats: grouped opencode statistics always report messages: 0 (Group.Messages never populated)

## Symptom

Every fire of `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py` prints, for all four queues:

```
Warning: Could not poll queue repo-health-code-pilot: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
Warning: Could not poll queue repo-health-opencode-pilot: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
Warning: Could not poll queue repo-health-openchamber-pilot: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
Warning: Could not poll queue repo-health-nix-pilot: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

and reports `candidates: []`, `stuck_bound: []` for every queue.

## Cause

`fetch_claimed_rows()` (poll.py:288) runs:

```
repo-queue list --queue <queue> --status claimed
```

and then `json.loads(result.stdout)`. But `~/fleet-brokers/bin/repo-queue` `list` emits a **human-readable table**, not JSON. There is no JSON mode in the CLI either:

```
$ repo-queue list --queue repo-health-code-pilot --status claimed --json
repo-queue: unrecognized argument: --json
$ ... --format json   -> unrecognized argument
$ ... --output json   -> unrecognized argument
```

So `json.loads` always raises and every queue contributes zero rows.

## Impact

This is not a transient outage — the claimed set is large. At fire time 2026-11-08T05:45Z the four queues held **37 claimed tasks** (code 20+, opencode 7, openchamber 3, nix 6). The claimant cannot see any of them, so:

- **Candidate discovery is blind fleet-wide.** Any claimed, lane-`opencode`, unbound task at a recorded yield stage is invisible and never

# mcpx(affected-tests): an `all:`-prefixed //go:embed pattern never matches — edits to the embedded opencode skills select no tests at all

## Summary

`pkgs/mcpx/scripts/affected-tests.py` maps a changed non-Go file to the package that embeds it (`embedded_owners`, :312), so an edit to an embedded input selects that package's T0/T1 commands. The matcher builds its candidate prefix from the raw embed pattern text (`base = pat` / `pkg_dir + "/" + pat`, :337-338) and never strips Go's `all:` pattern prefix. ## Summary

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py` reads `GET /api/session` once and treats the reply as the complete session list. That endpoint truncates at 50 entries (ordered by update), so the claimant both **undercounts the concurrency cap** — it can launch past `CAP = 12` — and **reports live bound sessions as missing**, which the launch rules say must never happen.

Observed 2026-11-03T04:42Z on the laptop server (`http://127.0.0.1:13420`):

- `GET /api/session` → exactly 50 sessions, 50 roots.
- Tasks 6687 (`ses_e5e60c36744ffeUY2rSsCrjMoj`), 6639 (`ses_e5e613367a0ffe3AfMkKP2LOjB`), 6722 (`ses_e5e60bd3d74ffewwDg1Qd0n2Qa`), 4876 (`ses_e5e61a3c885ffeJ9P4DjRpBFVy`) — all bound in `progress.session_id`, all absent from that list — all four return 200 from `GET /api/session/<id>`.

## Impact

1. **Cap overcount of room.** `summarize_cap()` ([poll.py:112-128](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py#L112-L128)) intersects the 50-row page with `/api/session/active`. Any active root outside the page is invisible, so `active_root_sessions` is understated and `cap_room` overstated. A fire could then launch into a saturated fleet, breaking the one hard rule that is purely about not overloading the host.

## Root cause

Mistral meters per **key**, not by call metadata. `vibe-direct` resolves its credential exactly like the `vibe` binary \u2014 env `MISTRAL_API_KEY` first, then `~/.vibe/.env`, then the OS keyring (`ai.mistral.vibe`). The home-manager `ExecStartPre` materializer exported the Bitwarden `mistral.api-key` value \u2014 the account **API key** (sha256 fp `144cdb68\u2026`, the same value as the enrolled `mistral` integration credential) \u2014 into the server unit env, so every vibe-direct request spent the API key and billed the $15 API budget. The keyring sign-in key (fp `b782943c\u2026`) is a different key and is the one that bills the Vibe plan.

Proven empirically 2026-11-06: the real `vibe` CLI succeeds on the keyring key while the API budget is exhausted; the same CLI forced onto the server env key returns the exact production error `402 billing_api_budget_exhausted`. Attribution: on 2026-11-05, while vibe-direct carried the deepseek-flash-plan load, 8,693 vibe-direct attempts went to Mistral, 8,660 of them inside the 16%->100% burn window (22:45Z wall) \u2014 yes, our own mis-keyed traffic burned the API pool.

# opencode-usage-export: state.json valid-but-wrong-shape JSON wedges every tick (null) or fabricates a store move (non-string storePath)

`pm-stack/opencode-usage-export/opencode-usage-export.mjs` reads its own
`state.json` (the out-dir file recording `{ storePath, lastTickAt }` from the
previous tick) with a bare parse and no shape validation:

- `readState` (`:303-305`) returns `JSON.parse(await readFile(...))` verbatim;
  its `catch` returns `{}` only for a *parse* failure. Valid JSON of the wrong
  shape passes straight through.
- `run()` then dereferences it unchecked (`:341`): `previousPath: state.storePath ?? null`.
  When `state.json` contains the JSON literal `null`, that is
  `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'storePath')` — a raw `TypeError`
  that the outer catch wraps as `read-failed` (exit 6).
- `resolveStore` (`:188`) trusts the type of `previousPath`:
  `previousPath && previousPath !== winner.path ? { from: previousPath, to: winner.path } : null`.
  A non-string `storePath` (e.g. `123`) is truthy and unequal to the winner
  path, so the success document reports a store move that never happened.

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` (HEAD `9f5a92057d`, restored by #7290) has the correct create → verify-location → bind ordering, but **stops after bind**. Step 4d builds the worker prompt as a string and never delivers it:

# claimant.py:474-489

prompt = f"""
Execute queue task {task_id}
...
"""
# In a real implementation, this would send the prompt via the session API

**PM-12 — /v1/exec runs are marked ephemeral.** `execsvc.scriptEnv` never set `MCPX_EPHEMERAL`, so the generated client never sent `x-mcpx-ephemeral`, `ReleaseCaller` never saw an ephemeral caller, and session-scoped instances (browsers) waited for idle reaping. `scriptEnv` now sets it with the CLI's rule: ephemeral unless the caller named a session (a named session may be shared and must outlive the run). ## Summary

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` at HEAD (`b5ddb39744`) reads the mode in `main()` and then only uses it for one thing: whether to run `supervision_step()`. It is **never consulted before a launch**.

```python
# claimant.py:512-550
mode = read_mode()
if mode == "live":
    supervision_step(mode)
...
launched, skips = launch_step(mode, cap_room)   # mode is passed and ignored
```

`launch_step(mode, cap_room)` takes `mode` as a parameter and never reads it. The body goes straight from the cap check to `POST /api/session` and `repo-queue bind`.

The task packet (`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/prompt.md`, §MODE) is explicit: "In shadow mode ... Never claim, bind, launch, or mutate a task in shadow mode." The living fire instruction is equally explicit that shadow is the default when `~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/mode` is absent.

## Reproduction (verified 2026-11-08, laptop)

Patched `read_mode` → `"shadow"`, `run_poll` → one valid `handed_off` candidate, and stubbed `subprocess.run` to record argv:

```
$ python3 <stub harness invoking claimant.main()>
OpenCode claimant starting in shadow mode
Running gate step...
Running cap step...
Cap room: 36 sessions available

Companion to developing-today/opencode#1468 (merged), which re-homes this door's Muse → credential-store token sync into the fork (`credential/codex-sync` in `@opencode/core`, opencode#1154).

## Change

`CODEX_PROXY_TOKEN_SYNC=0` turns this door's token sync off:

- `syncCodexTokensToOpenCode()` returns immediately when the variable is `0` (covers all three call sites: listen, per-request background refresh, and the 5-minute interval).

With the variable unset (the default), behavior is exactly today's — the sync keeps running until cutover.

## Why

At the #1154 cutover, the in-fork sync becomes the sole writer of the store's `openai` credential row. The two syncs must never write in alternation (the door writes a synthetic +30d expiry; the fork writes the true JWT expiry). The deploy track performs the cutover by adding `CODEX_PROXY_TOKEN_SYNC=0` to the `codex-proxy` unit's `Environment` in `home/common/default.nix` and restarting the door, after a server build containing opencode#1468 is deployed. The full sequence is recorded on opencode#1154. This PR intentionally does **not** make that unit change — it only adds the switch.

`node --test bin/codex-proxy.test.mjs` — 26/26 pass, including a new test (sync off: seeded credential row untouched, disabled line logged, no "updated" line) and both pre-existing #2533 sync tests unchanged.

## Summary

`iso()` in the aggregator's OpenCode session mapper converts a server-supplied millisecond timestamp with no range/finite gate, so one session whose `time.updated` (or `time.created`) is beyond the valid `Date` range makes `mapServerSessions` throw — and every caller fails soft at the whole-server level, so that one bad session silently drops **all** sessions from that OpenCode server from the attention feed and the durable registry.

## Evidence (main `5a34fa70`)

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/opencode.ts:86-87`:
  ```ts
  const iso = (ms: number | undefined): string | null =>
    typeof ms === "number" && ms > 0 ? new Date(ms).toISOString() : null;
  ```
  `typeof` + `> 0` admit `1e16`, `Number.MAX_VALUE`, and `Infinity`-adjacent magnitudes. JS `Date` is only valid to ±8.64e15 ms; `new Date(1e16).toISOString()` throws `RangeError: Invalid Date`. (JSON cannot carry `Infinity`, but it happily carries `1e16`.)
- The throw sites are unguarded: entry construction in `mapOne` (`opencode.ts:174` `createdAt: iso(s.time?.created)`, `:179` `lastActivityAt: iso(s.time?.updated)`) and the long-running-call stamp at `:255`. `mapOne`/`mapServerSessions` have no per-session try/catch — one throw aborts the whole map.
- The bad session is reliably *included* before it throws: the attention filter at `opencode.ts:146` is `now - s.time.updated <= ATTENTION_WINDOW_MS`, and for a huge future `updated` that difference is negative, so the session passes the filter and sorts firs
title: aggregator(opencode): iso() throws RangeError on out-of-range server timestamps — one bad session drops every session from that server

## Finding

The stale-branch cleanup workflow deletes candidates in a bare loop under `set -euo pipefail`, with no per-branch failure handling. One failed `git push origin --delete` aborts the whole run: later candidates are never attempted, the finish line never prints, and the same undeletable branch (ruleset protection, a concurrent delete, a transient push error) can starve every later candidate on every subsequent daily live run.

This is one cross-repo set — the workflow is byte-identical in the three repos below; file/fix it as a set, not per-repo duplicates.

## Evidence

- Source PRs (this repo): PR #1464 created the workflow; PR #1493 (`ci: run branch cleanup daily`, head `494e6dd5`) changed the schedule to daily, and its body states `BRANCH_CLEANUP_LIVE` has been set to true and verified — so scheduled runs perform live deletions daily.
- Current main `b2adaf47` (developing-today/code), `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml`: `set -euo pipefail` at line 46; deletion loop at lines 150–159 with a bare `git push origin --delete "$branch"` at line 155 and no guard, failure collection, or `|| true`.
- Same loop, verified on current main today: developing-today/opencode (`9ba2221f`, workflow lines 46 and 155) and developing-today/openchamber (`93027f59`, lines 46 and 155).
- Mechanism: under `set -e`, a failing command in the loop body (not in a condition) terminates the script immediately — later loop iterations never run. This exact mechanism was reproduced and confirm

## Summary

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/prompt.md` tells the claimant to create the worker session with a **top-level** `directory`:

```
POST /api/session with JSON body {"directory": <the repo's laptop primary>, "title": ..., "model": {...}, "agent": "build"}
```
(prompt.md:79-82)

The v2 OpenCode server does not accept a top-level `directory`. `session.create` decodes `location` (`Location.PublicRef` = `{directory}`) and strips unknown keys, so the field is silently dropped and the session is created at the server default location — `/home/user` — not the repo primary.

## Evidence

- `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts:221-234` — `session.create` payload is `{id, parentID, title, agent, model, location, metadata, permissions, subagentPolicy}`; there is no `directory` field.

## Summary

The zero-message verification in `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` (prompt.md step 1a, the #4758 / design #4912 recovery rule) calls an endpoint the v2 server does not have:

```
claimant.py:253  GET http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session/<id>/messages
```

The live server serves the **singular** `/message` (returning `{"data": [...], "cursor": ...}`). `/messages` is a **404 with an empty body** — verified on `http://127.0.0.1:13420` on 2026-11-08:

```
GET /api/session/ses_e5e441ca753ffdMse0Sd5IZ977/message   -> 200  data[50], cursor
GET /api/session/ses_e5e441ca753ffdMse0Sd5IZ977/messages  -> 404  (empty body)
```

`poll.py` and the fire probe already use the singular form (`fire-probe.py` `session_messages()`); only `claimant.py` — and the stub in `test/test_claimant.py:75`, which pins the wrong path — use `/messages`.

## Why this is fail-open, not merely inert

The block at `claimant.py:250-265` is:

```python
messages_response = subprocess.run(["curl", "-s", "-m", "5",
    f"http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session/{session_id}/messages"], ...)
if messages_response.returncode == 0:
    message_count = len(json.loads(messages_response.stdout or "[]"))
    if message_count == 0:
        recovery_candidates.append(...)
```

`curl -s` exits **0** on a 404, and the 404 body is empty, so:

1. `returncode == 0` → true,
2. `stdout or "[]"` → `"[]"` (the `or` was written for a timeout producing empty output),
3. `message_count == 0` → **every** stuck-bound row passes th

## Problem

`pkgs/opencode-config-normalize/normalize.sh` silently deletes every agent definition from a config that has an `agents` key but no `agent` key — which is exactly the shape OpenChamber's v1→v2 migration produces (the script's own header: OpenChamber migrates `agent` -> `agents`). The script reports "repaired" and exits 0 while the user's agents vanish, so the v1 CLI loses all its agent definitions — the opposite of the script's purpose.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `5a34fa70`)

- `normalize.sh:52-68` (embedded Python): when `'agents' in doc`, it computes `merged = {**agents, **agent}` and, if `merged != agent`, tries to splice the merged map into the existing `"agent"` block with the regex `"agent"(\s*):\s*\{.*?\n  \}` (lines 61-65). When there is **no** `"agent"` key, that regex cannot match (`"agents"` does not match `"agent"` + closing quote), so nothing is inserted and `n = 0`.
- The drop on line 67 then runs **unconditionally**: `re.subn(r'\n\s*"agents"\s*:\s*\{.*?\n  \},?', '', out, count=1, ...)` removes the `agents` block regardless of whether the merge splice succeeded, and sets `changed`, so the mutilated text is written after only a parse check (lines 73-79) that cannot detect the loss.
- Probe (this run, `/tmp/probe-laneB-normalize/`, script run with `OPENCODE_CONFIG` pointed at a copy): input with only `agents` (`build` + `plan` entries) and `plugins` came out as just `{ "$schema": ..., "plugin": ["opencode-plugin-x"] }` — both agents gone,
title: opencode-config-normalize: agents-only config silently loses every agent — the agents block is dropped even when the merge splice never lands

Observed 2026-10-29 on amd (laptop) by Muse, while verifying the Codex pool after a fresh `codex login`.

## Symptom

After `codex login` refreshed `~/.codex/auth.json` (2026-10-30T02:51:23Z), the laptop codex-proxy's built-in 5-minute `syncCodexTokensToOpenCode` did NOT update the OpenCode credential store. The active `openai` credential row still held a stale token (matching neither the old nor the fresh Codex token) until it was synced by hand. The proxy process runs the current script (since Oct 28), syncs at startup and every 5 minutes, and showed no error anywhere — the failure is invisible by design.

## Root cause (diagnosed + reproduced 2026-10-29)

`bin/codex-proxy.mjs`, `syncCodexTokensToOpenCode`:

```js
execSync(`python3 -c ${JSON.stringify(script)}`, { stdio: 'ignore' });
```

1. **The sync can never run.** `JSON.stringify(script)` encodes the Python script's newlines as literal two-character `\n` sequences. The shell, inside double quotes, does not turn `\n` into a newline, so `python3 -c` receives the whole script as one physical line full of literal `\n`. Python dies instantly with `SyntaxError: unexpected character after line continuation character`. Reproduced in isolation against a scratch sqlite DB with the exact construction from the proxy: same SyntaxError, DB unchanged.
2. **The failure is swallowed twice.** `stdio: 'ignore'` discards the child's stderr, and the surrounding `catch (err) { // Non-fatal background sync }` discards the throw. A failed syn
title: fix(codex-proxy): token sync to OpenCode store never runs — JSON.stringify shell quoting kills the Python child, and the error is swallowed

## Finding (from PR review, never addressed)

`delete_top_level_entry` in `pkgs/opencode-config-normalize/normalize.sh` finds the start of a preceding block comment with a plain backward `rfind('/*')`. When the block comment before the final legacy `agent` entry itself contains literal `/*` text — e.g. `/* example syntax: /* text */` — the scan selects the delimiter *inside* the comment rather than its actual opening. The next scan iteration then encounters the remaining comment text and returns `None`, so normalization exits 1 without repairing the file. The pre-existing regex implementation handled this layout, so previously supported commented configs regressed.

## Summary

Seven of the nine `bin/*-proxy.mjs` chat proxies **crash the whole process** on a
`POST /v1/chat/completions` whose body is valid JSON but not an object — the
literal `null`. Each handler `JSON.parse`s the body inside a try/catch (so
malformed JSON correctly gets a 400), but then dereferences the parsed value
without checking it is an object, so `null` throws a `TypeError` outside any
guard and Node exits. One malformed request from any client therefore kills a
long-lived fleet proxy until its supervisor restarts it.

The other two proxies already do this right and are the in-repo pattern to copy:

- `bin/clef-proxy.mjs:211` — `if (!body || typeof body !== 'object')` → 400
  "Invalid JSON body: expected an object", process stays up.
- `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs:709` — `if (!isPlainObject(body))` → 400
  "request body must be a JSON object", process stays up.

In pm-dispatch (`pm-stack/dispatch/src/server.ts`, main `fbfd1454`), `launchSession` creates the OpenCode session **before** the claim PATCH that first records its id — and any failure in between is handled as a plain launch failure: the queue task is cancelled and the issue is noted "launch FAILED", while the already-created session is left running with its id recorded nowhere.

## Problem

`mapServerSessions` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/opencode.ts) treats an in-range **future** `time.updated` stamp as fresh forever: the freshness inclusion is one-sided, so a session dated days or years ahead stays in the attention feed, sorts to the top, and can crowd genuinely recent sessions out of the detailed cap.

## Evidence (main `687ac07a`)

- `validMs` (opencode.ts:100-101) accepts any finite stamp `0 < ms <= 8.64e15` — including stamps far in the future. It gates both `iso()` and the freshness inclusion, per its own comment.

## Problem

The OpenCode Go quota extractor pairs each workspace with its monthly reset by **global position in the section**, not by the paragraph the reset appears in. One missing or one extra `monthly reset …` line silently shifts both workspaces' reset dates — each pool renders the other's reset, or a stale historical one, with no error anywhere.

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-extract.ts`, `goWorkspace` (:152-176):

```ts
// Resets appear in the same paragraph order as the workspaces.
const resets = [...s.matchAll(/monthly reset (\w{3}) (\d{1,2}), (\d{2}:\d{2}) UTC/gi)];
const r = name === "Personal" ? resets[0] : resets[1];
```

Both Go pools share the one `### OpenCode Go` section (`POOL_SPECS`, :276/:284 — the same `sectionOf` text is passed to both extractors). The workspace percentages are matched per-workspace by name, but the resets are collected section-wide and indexed `[0]`/`[1]`. The pairing holds only while every workspace paragraph carries exactly one reset line and nothing else in the section mentions one — and the quota view this parses is a human document that, per this file's own header, "preserves dated observations", so extra dated reset mentions in the section are expected over time.

## Evidence (verified on main be7cf629)

Probe on the laptop driving the **real** `extractQuotaPools` from `quota-extract.ts` (sha256 `29729137…`, identical in both clones; probe + log in the fleet bookkeeping `probe-2026-10-28-laneA-goreset/`, run twice with identical o
title: aggregator: OpenCode Go reset dates are paired by section position, not by workspace — one missing or extra 'monthly reset' line shifts both workspaces' resets

A task can be **requeued while a claimant-bound session is still live or while a
dead binding still exists**, and nothing clears `progress.session_id`:

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/install.mjs` — the installer that writes the #3026 claimant scheduled task into the laptop's real OpenChamber project store — performs **no argument validation**. `main()` (install.mjs:65-71) collects only the spellings it knows:

## Finding

PR #431 single-sources the codex-proxy port by changing the `openai-codex` provider's baseURL in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` from the hardcoded `http://127.0.0.1:18744/v1` to `http://127.0.0.1:{env:CODEX_PROXY_PORT}/v1`. The only place the new variable is set is `home.sessionVariables` (`home/common/default.nix`, from the single `codexProxyPort` definition) — i.e. it exists only in processes that inherit a home-manager shell session's environment.

OpenCode's `{env:VAR}` substitution has **no fallback**: a missing variable substitutes the empty string. In developing-today/opencode, `packages/core/src/config/variable.ts` (substitute function): `const value = (input.env?.[name] ?? process.env[name]) || ""`. So any opencode process launched without `CODEX_PROXY_PORT` in its environment gets baseURL `http://127.0.0.1:/v1` — a dead provider, and exactly the "looks like a network/auth problem" failure mode PR #431 set out to eliminate. The proxy script itself keeps a fallback (`bin/codex-proxy.mjs:7`: `process.env.CODEX_PROXY_PORT || '18744'`); after this PR the client side no longer has one, so the two sides can now disagree in the opposite direction: proxy listening on 18744, client dialling port "".

## Evidence

## Summary

`bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs`'s window-time parser accepts out-of-range times and silently reinterprets them: `parseHHMM` (bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs:398-401) only checks the shape `^([0-9]{1,2}):([0-9]{2})$` and returns `hour * 60 + minute` with no range check, so `24:60` parses to 1500 and `99:99` to 6039. Nothing else validates the windows either — `normalizeWindowGate` (:372-377) only extracts the gate name/invert flag, and the window definitions come straight from config (`model_route_windows`, :175).

## Verified behavior (this run)

Probe on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-02-laneB-routewindow/`) extracted `parseHHMM` + `windowActive` verbatim from the real file @ 6cdfaee0 (md5 c7ad071278474a5b4bfe0a181714cc0e) and ran them:

- `parseHHMM('09:30') = 570` (control, correct); `parseHHMM('24:60') = 1500`; `parseHHMM('99:99') = 6039` — all accepted.
- Window `99:99`–`99:98` (a wrapping window) is **active at Mon 12:00 UTC**: the wrap branch (`mins < end`, :443-447) is true for every real wall minute (max 1439 < 6038), so a nonsense window is effectively always-on — and with `invert: true` on the gate, always-off.
- Window `25:00`–`26:00` is **never active** (no wall minute reaches 1500 in the non-wrapping branch) — a typo'd window silently kills the route target, or, inverted, makes it permanently eligible.
- Window `09:00`–`24:60` behaves as if it had no end (active at 23:30), silently extending a curfew-style gate past its intent.

## Why it matters
title: opencode-route-proxy: window times are never range-checked — parseHHMM accepts 24:60 and 99:99, so a typo'd window silently becomes always-on, always-off, or end-less

## Problem

When `pkgs/opencode-config-normalize/normalize.sh` does repair `opencode.jsonc`, its write path discards the file's existing permissions and breaks symlinks: a `0600` config comes back `0644` (umask default), and a symlinked config is replaced by a brand-new regular file at the link path while the link target keeps the unrepaired v2 keys forever.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `fc88d0a9`, script sha256 `c59dd79b…`)

- `normalize.sh:126-128`: the repaired text is written to a fresh sibling temp file and moved over the config —
  ```python
  tmp = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + '.normalize-tmp')
  tmp.write_text(out)
  tmp.replace(path)
  ```
  Nothing copies the original file's mode onto `tmp`, and `Path.replace` on a symlinked `path` replaces the symlink itself, not its target. Nothing in the script checks `path.is_symlink()` or `stat` mode.
- Laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneA-normalize/`, verbatim copy of the script, sha-matched to main):
  - Case B: a `chmod 600` config needing repair → repaired correctly, but `stat` afterwards shows `644`.
  - Case C: config as a symlink to `target.jsonc` needing repair → after the run the link path is a regular file (`-rw-r--r--`, no longer a symlink) holding the repaired content, while `target.jsonc` still contains the unrepaired `"plugins"` key.

## Why it matters

An opencode config can carry provider credentials, so silently widening `0600` → `0644` exposes them to other local users — the same defect
title: opencode-config-normalize: the repair write discards the config's permissions (0600 -> 0644) and silently severs a symlinked config — tmp+replace with no mode copy and no symlink handling (normalize.sh:126-128)

## Finding

PR #357 (https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/357, commit 55efb43d, merged in 238adf46) split `jules.yml`'s shared workflow-level concurrency group into per-job groups "keyed by its target" (its words) — but the new `manual` job's group is a constant, and it is the one job whose target varies on every run: the dispatch `prompt`. The same constant-group-over-varying-inputs pattern also sits in four sibling Jules workflows across three repos (listed below); none of them sets `queue:`, so GitHub's default `queue: single` semantics apply.

With `cancel-in-progress: false` and the default single queue, each group holds one running run plus one pending run. A third arrival in the group silently cancels the pending one — it shows as "cancelled", produces no failure, and its Jules task never starts. This is the exact failure mode already fixed for other workflows in code #302 (auto-assign), openchamber #77 (`queue: max`), and dezren39/nix #413/#425 — the Jules dispatch paths were left out.

# opencode-usage-export: `--db`/`--out-dir` values are never validated — a trailing or empty `--db` silently exports the default store, a trailing `--out-dir` silently writes the default out dir, and a flag-like value crashes `run()` with no failure document

## Summary

`pm-stack/opencode-usage-export/opencode-usage-export.mjs` validates none of the values of its two path flags. In `parseArgs` (lines 320–330 at `def55caf48`):

```js
if (a === "--db") args.db = argv[++i];
else if (a === "--out-dir") args.outDir = argv[++i];
```

- A **trailing** `--db` sets `args.db = undefined`; `run()` then computes `explicit = args.db ?? env.OPENCODE_USAGE_DB ?? null` and falls back to the default candidate stores — the tick exports a *different store than the operator named*, exit 0, `status: "ok"`.
- An **empty** `--db ""` sets `args.db = ""`; `explicit ? [explicit] : defaultCandidatePaths(home)` treats `""` as absent — same silent fallback.
- A **trailing** `--out-dir` sets `args.outDir = undefined`; the document, `state.json`, and history are silently written to the default `~/atlas/opencode-usage-export/` instead of the requested directory, exit 0.
- A **flag-like** value (`--db --out-dir <path>`) consumes `--out-dir` as the db path and leaves `<path>` as a bare token, so `parseArgs` throws `unknown argument: <path>` — and because `parseArgs(argv)` is called *before* `run()`'s try block (line ~340), the throw escapes `run()` entirely: no failure document is written, the previous tick'
title: opencode-usage-export: --db/--out-dir values are never validated — a trailing or empty --db silently exports the default store, a trailing --out-dir silently writes the default out dir, and a flag-like value crashes run() with no failure document

# aggregator(opencode): mapServerSessions never validates the v2 wire containers — a non-array `data` on any endpoint, or one null session entry, throws out of the mapper and drops every session from that server; an id-less entry fabricates an undefined-sessionId row

## Summary

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/opencode.ts` maps an OpenCode v2 server's responses into feed entries with no validation of the wire containers or the session entries themselves. `mapServerSessions` (opencode.ts:116) trusts that every endpoint's `data` is an array and that every session entry is an object with an `id`:

- The session list is used unguarded: `const sessions = list.data` (:125), the token loop dereferences `s.tokens` on every entry (:145-148), and the inclusion filter/sort dereference `s.time` / `s.id` (:150-157).
- The permission list is iterated unguarded (:139, `for (const p of permResp?.data ?? [])`).
- In `mapOne`, the message list is iterated unguarded (:225, `for (const m of data)` where `data = msgs?.data ?? []`, :213).

Any of these shapes therefore throws a `TypeError` out of `mapServerSessions` instead of returning entries or `null`. Both callers are deliberately fail-soft per server — the collector wraps the call in one catch and logs "sandbox server read failed; attention empty" (scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts:464-502), and live.ts catches around `laptopSessions()` / `laptopMapped()` and marks the laptop part failed (live.ts:907-918, :1012-1019) — so the throw drops **ever
title: aggregator(opencode): mapServerSessions never validates the v2 wire containers — a non-array data on any endpoint, or one null session entry, throws out of the mapper and drops every session from that server; an id-less entry fabricates an undefined-sessionId row
